body:
November 16, 2026 | Read Online ( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/e5uzom7wqph7he9xnvqu8h888eomzblh0g46q/25h2hoh3506rgph3h4/aHR0cHM6Ly9ja2FyY2hpdmUuY29tL2IvNXF1dmg3aDBwZTl4a3VwNXh4ZDUyYTk5OWdsNHphbmhnMG1wbw== )

From Catherine
--------------

Support True the Vote’s work ( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/e5uzom7wqph7he9xnvqu8h888eomzblh0g46q/qvh8h7hdx2zgv9blhk/aHR0cHM6Ly90cnVldGhldm90ZS5vcmcvZG9uYXRl )

Hi Friend —

In 1905, the philosopher George Santayana wrote in The Life of Reason, “Those who cannot remember the past are condemned to repeat it.” So. True.

Now, as we find our way through the fog of 2026, we keep stumbling over the wreckage of 2020.

Americans are still grappling with what happened six years ago and who answered for it (which is a very short list). I remember how the FBI and its agents provocateurs, inside and outside the Bureau, courted True the Vote. They wanted to hear what we’d found. Yet the more compelling the evidence of election crimes we turned over, the more we were treated like criminals ourselves. Covering it up and moving on suited the Swamp, the political class, and powerful interests around the world. And America was left with unlearned lessons and unanswered questions.

Now here we are again.
----------------------

By the eve of Election Day, this cycle's spending was nearly $12 billion. On what? Primarily on advertising, including payments to social media influencers to repeat whatever message they were paid to promote, events, and salaries.

How much was set aside to detect exploitation of election processes? Now that the polls are closed and certification is approaching, what will the candidates do, and what will they invest, to find out what happened in the 2026 midterms?

They have the money, the data, the technology, and the access. Will they dig in this time? If so, will they publish what they find, even if it disappoints their own side? If they uncover wrongdoing, will they see the fight through? And where should they look first?

In our opinion, any investigation must begin with an assessment of the voter rolls and who actually voted, but that’s step one of many, and no step should be skipped. Some social media influencers are now arguing that national turnout trends rule out software manipulation. I think it’s way too early to close that question.

Consider what we’ve learned about federal systems over the past few months.

In August, the Justice Department’s ATF confirmed a breach of an older system containing investigative information. An FBI affidavit also disclosed earlier intrusions at the National Institutes of Health and three Department of Energy national laboratories.

In September, the FBI’s recruiting portal was compromised. The Pentagon disclosed that unauthorized users had access to personnel data for roughly nine months. That breach affected about three million people.

In October, data on more than 40,000 Homeland Security personnel appeared online. An attack on a contractor interrupted federal telephone support for truckers.

A week before the election, an attempted breach disrupted the Federal Election Commission’s campaign-finance filing system.

Then came Friday. The secretaries of Transportation and Homeland Security told us the FAA had ordered a nationwide ground stop affecting an estimated 36,000 flights. A contractor was replacing old copper lines with fiber when communications and radar feeds became unreliable (!??!)

Now, let’s look — honestly — at our elections.

Too many processes are vulnerable, too much equipment is old, and the people responsible for running it get too little support. And online data can be hacked and manipulated, no point in saying it could never happen in elections, because it’s happening everywhere.

So what are we going to do differently now to keep the failures we remember from becoming the failures we repeat in 2028?

Audits Are Beginning
--------------------

( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/e5uzom7wqph7he9xnvqu8h888eomzblh0g46q/9qhzhnhd730kxeu9h3/aHR0cHM6Ly9hdWRpdHMudHJ1ZXRoZXZvdGUub3Jn )
States are beginning their risk-limiting audits and hand counts. The procedures are documented and prescribed in advance. We built a guide so you can find the official notices, learn how to observe, and read the findings for yourself. Find your state at audits.truethevote.org ( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/e5uzom7wqph7he9xnvqu8h888eomzblh0g46q/n2hohvhvd5mwgdt6hg/aHR0cHM6Ly9hdWRpdHMudHJ1ZXRoZXZvdGUub3JnLw== ).

But all audits are not the same, so before you read an audit’s conclusions, ask one question. What did it actually examine?

Case in point: Texas’s first statewide risk-limiting audit begins November 19. Officials will examine randomly selected paper ballots to check the reported outcome of selected contests. The procedures are public. Anyone, including bad actors, can study those procedures and see where the review stops. And just because a selection of sampled ballot agrees with the count, that tells us almost nothing about the accuracy of the voter rolls, the eligibility of voters, or who had access to election systems. Each of those questions requires its own investigation.

Get involved where you can
--------------------------

We need tests to determine whether software altered a count. Ask to see the ballots, the system records, and the work that reconciles them. And go back to 2024. The DOJ ordered most states to preserve all their 2024 records, so begin as far back as you can, bring in professionals in the space and examine everything .... publicly. A national turnout chart can’t settle this. Radical transparency can.

And local engagement matters: when we exposed Konnech (the elections software company that was running American elections out of Beijing) the federal government did nothing but aid in the coverup.

Citizens took action, spread the word, and counties across the country (some, though not all) cancelled their contracts. The lesson is that real change will likely begin with your county and state.

Start now.
----------

As I said last week, we’re going back to old-school organizing and training. Human to human. We’ll put the technology in our volunteers’ hands and give them an organizer’s toolbox they can use in their own communities.

( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/e5uzom7wqph7he9xnvqu8h888eomzblh0g46q/48hvhehmoqvzqzsxh7/aHR0cHM6Ly9ydW1ibGUuY29tL3Y3aWNmNmUtbGliZXJ0eXdvcmtzLXdvcmtzaG9wLXB0LTEuaHRtbA== )
Weekly workshops begin Tuesday, November 17 at 1p eastern, and they’re for citizens across the country. They'll be live, but definitely available to watch later. Our first series will teach you how to audit voter rolls. We’ll walk through which records to request, how to read a voter record entry, and how to document a discrepancy your county can investigate.

You can start today with your own name and voters at your address. In the past few weeks, more than 60,000 registration checks have been run through Scan. Check. Protect. and twenty-one percent of users reported a problem with their registration or voting record! Check your record with Scan. Check. Protect. ( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/e5uzom7wqph7he9xnvqu8h888eomzblh0g46q/wnh2hghqzvn9v5c7hx/aHR0cHM6Ly9zY2FuY2hlY2twcm90ZWN0Lm9yZw== )

America can fix these vulnerabilities before 2028.
--------------------------------------------------

This is correctable. It comes down to leadership, data, technology, steady oversight, communication, and public awareness of every step. It’s doable. What continues to be lacking is the political will to fund the work — real work, not “politico work” — and stay with it until it’s done.

We are fighting for leadership of the free world, while it is still free. Time to grow up.

That starts with the discipline to investigate and the honesty to say what can be proven, what remains uncertain, and what it will take to remove the uncertainty. Whatever the evidence proves wrong, we need the clarity and conviction to say so. When it exposes wrongdoing, we need a titanium spine to act.

Gird up, friends. It’s time to head towards into the arena.

Keep the faith. Never quit. Ephesians 6 FTW!

Ever onward —

P.S. True the Vote will be involved in Texas, organizing is happening now. We may take on projects elsewhere as other efforts come together. If something is taking shape in your county or state, please let us know. ( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/e5uzom7wqph7he9xnvqu8h888eomzblh0g46q/8ghqhoho4pzepptkh9/aHR0cHM6Ly9pbmZvQHRydWV0aGV2b3RlLm9yZw== )

P.S.S. I’ve given you my take on election integrity. There’s another part of the story. I believe there was fraud, as there is in every election. I also believe too many politicians have lost touch with the people they ask to represent. You can fill a voter’s mailbox with flyers and flood their phone with memes without ever hearing a word they have to say.

This country has serious problems. Thinking you already know what’s on people’s minds without bothering to ask them is the height of political arrogance.

Walk the blocks. Knock on doors. Hold a town hall and stay for the questions you’d rather duck. Then go do what you said you’d do.

Walk the talk. Or move aside. Please.

CA: Voters said yes...Judge said no.
------------------------------------

Nearly 56% of Shasta County voters approved Measure B, requiring voter ID, hand-counted ballots, and other election reforms. Now a judge has permanently struck it down, ruling that its provisions conflict with state law. Supporters are considering an appeal. We really are living in a bizarro world.

Don't forget! You can check your own voter registration record and your activity right now. Visit scancheckprotect.org ( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/e5uzom7wqph7he9xnvqu8h888eomzblh0g46q/wnh2hghqzvn9v5c7hx/aHR0cHM6Ly9zY2FuY2hlY2twcm90ZWN0Lm9yZw== ) and take three minutes to:

* Confirm your current record is accurate — your name, address, and status.
* See if your early vote was recorded — check back if your state hasn't reported yet.
* Verify that your address isn't being used as a voter trap house — after you pull up your record, check your current address and confirm you recognize anyone else who may be registered at your residence.
* Check the rolls in states where you used to live — old registrations often linger for years after you've moved, sometimes without your knowledge.
* Tell us what you found. Good or bad, we want to hear from you — and if something looks off, we're here to help you fix it.

Grounded in Truth
-----------------

A weekly word from the TTV team. Want one every day? Join us in TTV Now. ( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/e5uzom7wqph7he9xnvqu8h888eomzblh0g46q/dpheh0he3wvzw0hmh4/aHR0cHM6Ly9jb21tdW5pdHkudHR2bm93Lm9yZy9jaGVja291dC9iZWNvbWUtYS1tZW1iZXI= )

Father,

Thank You for Your sovereignty and for being our constant in a world that is constantly changing. Thank You that even in the middle of disappointment and uncertainty, the sun still rises and light replaces the darkness. Thank You for Your faithfulness that remains unchanged.

When disappointment weighs heavily on our hearts and confusion surrounds us, remind us that You are still on the throne. You are not surprised by the events of this world. You are not uncertain about what tomorrow holds. And Your plans for us, Your people, have not changed.

When fear or worries disrupt our peace, remind us that our victory is not found in things of this world. Our victory has already been secured through Jesus Christ. And no earthly power or government can take that away from us or overturn Your promises.

Our leaders come and go, but the sun still rises each morning. Your promises are unbreakable. And our hope is secure in You.

Give us wisdom to know how to move forward, courage to stand firm in our faith, and willing hearts to continue the work You have called us to do. Remind us that disappointment does not mean defeat and discouragement is not a reason to give up. There is still work to be done and there are still opportunities to shine Your light into the darkness.

We praise You because our calling has not changed, our purpose has not changed, and our King is still on the throne.I

n Jesus' Name, Amen.

~Jenna Riggs

For more prayers and encouragement from Jenna, join our Devotionals Space ( https://de717de0.click.kit-mail3.com/e5uzom7wqph7he9xnvqu8h888eomzblh0g46q/7qh7h8h9gpqvpwtzh6/aHR0cHM6Ly9jb21tdW5pdHkudHR2bm93Lm9yZy9jL2Rldm90aW9uYWxzLw== ) in the TTVN Community!

Until Next Week
---------------

Remember: you don't need a title, a law degree, or anyone's permission to get involved. You need awareness, courage, and the resolve to stay in it when others walk away.

True the Vote will keep doing our part. With faith as our foundation and patriots like you standing in the gap, we'll keep pressing for transparency, accountability, and an America we leave stronger than we found it.

Ever onward.

clean_body: November 16, 2026 | Read Online ( == ) From Catherine Support True the Vote’s work ( ) Hi Friend — In 1905, the philosopher George Santayana wrote in The Life of Reason, “Those who cannot remember the past are condemned to repeat it.” So. True. Now, as we find our way through the fog of 2026, we keep stumbling over the wreckage of 2020. Americans are still grappling with what happened six years ago and who answered for it (which is a very short list). I remember how the FBI and its agents provocateurs, inside and outside the Bureau, courted True the Vote. They wanted to hear what we’d found. Yet the more compelling the evidence of election crimes we turned over, the more we were treated like criminals ourselves. Covering it up and moving on suited the Swamp, the political class, and powerful interests around the world. And America was left with unlearned lessons and unanswered questions. Now here we are again. By the eve of Election Day, this cycle's spending was nearly $12 billion. On what? Primarily on advertising, including payments to social media influencers to repeat whatever message they were paid to promote, events, and salaries. How much was set aside to detect exploitation of election processes? Now that the polls are closed and certification is approaching, what will the candidates do, and what will they invest, to find out what happened in the 2026 midterms? They have the money, the data, the technology, and the access. Will they dig in this time? If so, will they publish what they find, even if it disappoints their own side? If they uncover wrongdoing, will they see the fight through? And where should they look first? In our opinion, any investigation must begin with an assessment of the voter rolls and who actually voted, but that’s step one of many, and no step should be skipped. Some social media influencers are now arguing that national turnout trends rule out software manipulation. I think it’s way too early to close that question. Consider what we’ve learned about federal systems over the past few months. In August, the Justice Department’s ATF confirmed a breach of an older system containing investigative information. An FBI affidavit also disclosed earlier intrusions at the National Institutes of Health and three Department of Energy national laboratories. In September, the FBI’s recruiting portal was compromised. The Pentagon disclosed that unauthorized users had access to personnel data for roughly nine months. That breach affected about three million people. In October, data on more than 40,000 Homeland Security personnel appeared online. An attack on a contractor interrupted federal telephone support for truckers. A week before the election, an attempted breach disrupted the Federal Election Commission’s campaign-finance filing system. Then came Friday. The secretaries of Transportation and Homeland Security told us the FAA had ordered a nationwide ground stop affecting an estimated 36,000 flights. A contractor was replacing old copper lines with fiber when communications and radar feeds became unreliable (!??!) Now, let’s look — honestly — at our elections. Too many processes are vulnerable, too much equipment is old, and the people responsible for running it get too little support. And online data can be hacked and manipulated, no point in saying it could never happen in elections, because it’s happening everywhere. So what are we going to do differently now to keep the failures we remember from becoming the failures we repeat in 2028? Audits Are Beginning ( ) States are beginning their risk-limiting audits and hand counts. The procedures are documented and prescribed in advance. We built a guide so you can find the official notices, learn how to observe, and read the findings for yourself. Find your state at audits.truethevote.org ( == ). But all audits are not the same, so before you read an audit’s conclusions, ask one question. What did it actually examine? Case in point: Texas’s first statewide risk-limiting audit begins November 19. Officials will examine randomly selected paper ballots to check the reported outcome of selected contests. The procedures are public. Anyone, including bad actors, can study those procedures and see where the review stops. And just because a selection of sampled ballot agrees with the count, that tells us almost nothing about the accuracy of the voter rolls, the eligibility of voters, or who had access to election systems. Each of those questions requires its own investigation. Get involved where you can We need tests to determine whether software altered a count. Ask to see the ballots, the system records, and the work that reconciles them. And go back to 2024. The DOJ ordered most states to preserve all their 2024 records, so begin as far back as you can, bring in professionals in the space and examine everything .... publicly. A national turnout chart can’t settle this. Radical transparency can. And local engagement matters: when we exposed Konnech (the elections software company that was running American elections out of Beijing) the federal government did nothing but aid in the coverup. Citizens took action, spread the word, and counties across the country (some, though not all) cancelled their contracts. The lesson is that real change will likely begin with your county and state. Start now. As I said last week, we’re going back to old-school organizing and training. Human to human. We’ll put the technology in our volunteers’ hands and give them an organizer’s toolbox they can use in their own communities. ( == ) Weekly workshops begin Tuesday, November 17 at 1p eastern, and they’re for citizens across the country. They'll be live, but definitely available to watch later. Our first series will teach you how to audit voter rolls. We’ll walk through which records to request, how to read a voter record entry, and how to document a discrepancy your county can investigate. You can start today with your own name and voters at your address. In the past few weeks, more than 60,000 registration checks have been run through Scan. Check. Protect. and twenty-one percent of users reported a problem with their registration or voting record! Check your record with Scan. Check. Protect. ( == ) America can fix these vulnerabilities before 2028. This is correctable. It comes down to leadership, data, technology, steady oversight, communication, and public awareness of every step. It’s doable. What continues to be lacking is the political will to fund the work — real work, not “politico work” — and stay with it until it’s done. We are fighting for leadership of the free world, while it is still free. Time to grow up. That starts with the discipline to investigate and the honesty to say what can be proven, what remains uncertain, and what it will take to remove the uncertainty. Whatever the evidence proves wrong, we need the clarity and conviction to say so. When it exposes wrongdoing, we need a titanium spine to act. Gird up, friends. It’s time to head towards into the arena. Keep the faith. Never quit. Ephesians 6 FTW! Ever onward — P.S. True the Vote will be involved in Texas, organizing is happening now. We may take on projects elsewhere as other efforts come together. If something is taking shape in your county or state, please let us know. ( == ) P.S.S. I’ve given you my take on election integrity. There’s another part of the story. I believe there was fraud, as there is in every election. I also believe too many politicians have lost touch with the people they ask to represent. You can fill a voter’s mailbox with flyers and flood their phone with memes without ever hearing a word they have to say. This country has serious problems. Thinking you already know what’s on people’s minds without bothering to ask them is the height of political arrogance. Walk the blocks. Knock on doors. Hold a town hall and stay for the questions you’d rather duck. Then go do what you said you’d do. Walk the talk. Or move aside. Please. -->Please Help Support Our Work ( ) Please Help Support Our Work ( ) Introducing LibertyWorks ( == ) Join us live on Tuesday, November 17th @1p eastern. Recording will also be available. ( == ) CA: Voters said yes...Judge said no. Nearly 56% of Shasta County voters approved Measure B, requiring voter ID, hand-counted ballots, and other election reforms. Now a judge has permanently struck it down, ruling that its provisions conflict with state law. Supporters are considering an appeal. We really are living in a bizarro world. Read More ( == ) ( ) Track Audits in Your State Wondering what's happening with post-election audits in your state? We've built a new 50-state guide bringing together audit practices, official 2026 updates, and published results. Find your state, follow the process, and see what's happening after the votes are cast. Track Your State ( ) ( == ) Don't forget! You can check your own voter registration record and your activity right now. Visit scancheckprotect.org ( == ) and take three minutes to: Confirm your current record is accurate — your name, address, and status. See if your early vote was recorded — check back if your state hasn't reported yet. Verify that your address isn't being used as a voter trap house — after you pull up your record, check your current address and confirm you recognize anyone else who may be registered at your residence. Check the rolls in states where you used to live — old registrations often linger for years after you've moved, sometimes without your knowledge. * Tell us what you found. Good or bad, we want to hear from you — and if something looks off, we're here to help you fix it. Tools for Your Toolkit You weren't meant to do this alone. Find your community, your tools, your purpose. -->Become a Member ( = ) Become a Member ( = ) Stay ahead of the legislation shaping your elections and know when it's time to act. -->Join LegiTrack ( ) Join LegiTrack ( ) Grounded in Truth A weekly word from the TTV team. Want one every day? Join us in TTV Now. ( = ) Father, Thank You for Your sovereignty and for being our constant in a world that is constantly changing. Thank You that even in the middle of disappointment and uncertainty, the sun still rises and light replaces the darkness. Thank You for Your faithfulness that remains unchanged. When disappointment weighs heavily on our hearts and confusion surrounds us, remind us that You are still on the throne. You are not surprised by the events of this world. You are not uncertain about what tomorrow holds. And Your plans for us, Your people, have not changed. When fear or worries disrupt our peace, remind us that our victory is not found in things of this world. Our victory has already been secured through Jesus Christ. And no earthly power or government can take that away from us or overturn Your promises. Our leaders come and go, but the sun still rises each morning. Your promises are unbreakable. And our hope is secure in You. Give us wisdom to know how to move forward, courage to stand firm in our faith, and willing hearts to continue the work You have called us to do. Remind us that disappointment does not mean defeat and discouragement is not a reason to give up. There is still work to be done and there are still opportunities to shine Your light into the darkness. We praise You because our calling has not changed, our purpose has not changed, and our King is still on the throne.I n Jesus' Name, Amen. ~Jenna Riggs For more prayers and encouragement from Jenna, join our Devotionals Space ( == ) in the TTVN Community! Until Next Week Remember: you don't need a title, a law degree, or anyone's permission to get involved. You need awareness, courage, and the resolve to stay in it when others walk away. True the Vote will keep doing our part. With faith as our foundation and patriots like you standing in the gap, we'll keep pressing for transparency, accountability, and an America we leave stronger than we found it. Ever onward. Stand With True the Vote ( ) We can't do this without you — and we wouldn't want to. Thank you for your support! BUT WAIT, THERE'S MORE! Dear Patriot,
Nearly twenty years in this work has taught me one rule about Washington: **When a door opens, someone is already pushing it shut.** Senator Rand Paul opened one for us. Send subpoena requests to his office . . . the one office in the Senate with sole power to issue them. **No reporter has ever held a key like this.** Since then, you and I have a responsibility to build something fast: A small team of researchers and professionals must be funded and put to work right now. Threads picked: the ballot cash. The border money. The Pfizer papers. And one twenty-year theory, at last ready for its test. Now for the truth about doors . . . Gavels change hands. Sessions end. And the first time a return comes back with a big name on it, they will push hard to shut this down. Harder than we have ever felt. **Senator Paul 's offer has no closing date printed on it. Washington will print one for us if we move slow.** So we will not move slow. If you have been waiting, **this is the moment.** [**Every gift, big or small, goes through that open door with us.**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNjIsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABCOcLVnjIBSbM-kRhKuWVkaJiS7wGNJOx6aIjGn5cLasOHvIoVnXlYeLwcXk_0xt1Xm6tJas8le2bpiLz9ocMkjILnjEV8nZQ1xTR0U) [**Give before the door closes.**](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNjIsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABCOcLVnkLq3FQ0RPLRAA9eCI9UVoL_QV_fd-OAghRqZ1HVNxXOfmf1NuvvG9-tGXyE49kYhHeCMBJhh8fr_-vWYF5DSnHzxeuOY3ATQ) **[GIVE BEFORE THE DOOR CLOSES](https://click.parlermailer.com/?qs=ABl7ImQiOjUwNjIsInQiOjc2NywicyI6MTJ9AAwAAAAABCOcLVnlcYiVpLVGarmqC-6M9-RX2HEKPIWRbi8zsDj5D0EMy7JsTIzqyQPrhiX7R-WUGAl-DXq8U4RGpV4mG8EK-0V_hTbAgtQeV7w)** Thank you for all that you do. I mean that more than you know.
In Truth, James O'Keefe Founder, O'Keefe Media Group

name: Ayanna Pressley
subject: If it were up to me, we’d use our majority to fight for:
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY JUSTICE DEMOCRATS
body:
Here's how I see things, Peter:

Republicans have spent the last two years flooding the zone with
lawlessness, cruelty, and corruption.

Voters had enough. They elected a majority of Democrats to Congress with a
mandate to match that energy — boldly and unapologetically.

We don’t do that by simply just being the adults in the room. We have to
prove that we’re FIGHTERS in the room.

So if it were up to me, we’d use our majority to fight for:

* Saving health care. Not just reversing Republicans’ cuts — advancing
Medicare for ALL. Passing national abortion protections. Not just
restoring what was stripped away — expanding reproductive rights.
* Stopping data centers. Putting real guardrails and oversight in place
over the AI industry.
* Enacting national voting rights and economic reparations for Black
people.
* Stop the genocide and end the wars.
* Abolishing ICE. Period.

Republicans showed us how they use their power to advance their agenda of
chaos and harm. I have stopped wondering how low they can go — and have
been focused on how hard we can fight.

This is the moment. We can’t waste it. We may not win every single fight —
but voters fully expect us to take those righteous fights on. And we must.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20261116-ap.Ib_3X6&refcode=em20261116-38435&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=1002&akid=38435%2E1203867%2EPlUMg0 ]We need to show that an agenda like this has real, public support.
So Peter, will you split a
donation between Justice Democrats and our campaign so we can fight hard
for our new Democratic majority to prioritize an agenda like this? Let’s
demonstrate how many people in Pennsylvania support this vision.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20261116-ap.Ib_3X6&refcode=em20261116-38435&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=1021&akid=38435%2E1203867%2EPlUMg0 ]Contribute $10

In solidarity,

Ayanna

Contribute to Justice Democrats: https://secure.actblue.com/donate/justicedemocrats?refcode=em20261116-38435-footer&t=1022&refcode2=38435_1203867_PlUMg0&akid=38435%2E1203867%2EPlUMg0

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: No te dejes
body:
My grandmother’s two words became something all of us said together.
# [](https://governorhinojosa.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
My abuela, Grandma Hinojosa, had a way of making everything sound like a scolding, even when it was pure love. And the thing she told me most often was:
_“No te dejes.”_
Don’t let them push you around. Know your worth, and fight for it.
Those were the first words I said when I launched this campaign. On my hardest days, I wore her ring and heard her voice. And on election night, I said them again, because I knew I wasn’t the only one who grew up hearing them. So many Latinas in Texas heard those same words from their own mothers and abuelas.
This year, Texas lived these words. The people who have been buying our politics in this state for too long spent hundreds of millions of dollars trying to push us around. They wrote us off over and over again. But we didn’t let them.
_**¡No nos dejamos!**_
[****](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261116_1_nonosdejamossticker.JglHI0&refcode=em20261116-2668&t=1&akid=2668%2E299639%2EVMJeDG)
[**Chip in anything you can, even just $1, to help cover printing and shipping, and we’ll send you this limited-edition “¡No Nos Dejamos!” sticker.**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261116_1_nonosdejamossticker.JglHI0&refcode=em20261116-2668&t=2&akid=2668%2E299639%2EVMJeDG)
There’s a reason the sticker doesn’t say “no te dejes.”
_No te dejes_ is something one person tells another: a grandmother to a granddaughter, a mom to her kid on the way out the door. _No nos dejamos_ is what happens when millions of people decide it together. **We didn’t let them push us around. We fought back. And we won.**
That’s what this sticker means. Big money tried to buy this election, and it couldn’t silence us. The lobbyists and billionaires who’ve run Austin for decades are learning that Texans know our worth.
So put it somewhere you’ll be proud to show it off: your truck, your laptop, your water bottle, your front door. Let every neighbor who walks by know that Texas doesn’t back down.
And let the powerful know we’re not done. Every time they try to push Texas families around, they’re going to get the same answer.
**[Chip in $1 or more and claim your “¡No Nos Dejamos!” sticker today.](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20261116_1_nonosdejamossticker.JglHI0&refcode=em20261116-2668&t=3&akid=2668%2E299639%2EVMJeDG)**
[Donate $5 »](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20261116_1_nonosdejamossticker.BGa0My&amount=5&refcode=em20261116-2668&t=22&akid=2668%2E299639%2EVMJeDG)
I think my grandmother would have loved this sticker. And she would be so proud of what we did together, Peter.
_No te dejes._ ¡No nos dejamos!
With gratitude,
Gina Hinojosa

Email us: [info@ginafortexas.com](mailto:info@ginafortexas.com)

And she would be so proud of what we did together, Peter. No te dejes. ¡No nos dejamos! With gratitude, Gina Hinojosa Email us: mailto:info@ginafortexas.com

## UPS, Copa Jets Collide at Miami Airport
A UPS cargo jet and a Copa Airlines plane carrying 172 people [collided while taxiing](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkD2u4yAURleDOyLANpCCYhp3b9oprRu4xHfEj4V59mT3o2QLr_909J3z52v9AkpUnr8ho4s1rgWvI2Hv2NZMkKl9lwtemY4NdvS11PyKqxJKcym51Cv4TieuEwzBmcmCeAzopLlPVmkt9LA5q6KyHo3Q3ngTTPQhCDAajTT3edYDuTdPSqmlmPU03lDPdzuGOD6CkSLObBIYqNd2-1upxPSqJ7aYaqMAN1_zkNzW-36w8RdTC1PLdV238vAfgfeAqeXtxdSSqofE1OLrDvx7P_ieoODBqZw1nRg4FZ6p1MZ9g2Pj10YJeYd_ROXJofMPk1Pp2Ap0qgUSB2p7bZ2pZbTWjmpiahmaC_tFKdGhDZvEMwOlz9n-w86nU_8DAAD__yVNlRs) at Miami International Airport on Saturday night. Two passengers were checked for minor injuries, and neither was hospitalized. Copa's 737, arriving from Panama City, struck the UPS 767's nose with its wingtip around 9:15 p.m. Controllers had told the UPS crew to yield, [the FAA said](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJyk0L2unDAUBOCnMZ1X_sEGCheRIrpNE0Up0TE-Xk5kMDLeJbz91e4r3Hqk0Xzz9z7dgRJtj1-woos5ThueR8JasUwrwUrluZ1wrXQssOOct7xecVJCWS4ll3aCudILpxaa4Lq2B-EbdLIb2l5ZK2yzOO21BuW9CYPvpInDjMKbQfW-kx5N25B790kprRTGtvqG1gy9DlH70EkRDWsFBqq53P5l2mK68gtLTLlQgNuc1ya5pdb9YPoHUyNTI_j57XhnTI1_fjM1PveD7wk25HPegQOVRBsePCZ6LJXPOSUKyCv8pxMu_rEzNR41l4vpkQLTP6XupVGD0k1xYT8pJTpsx1rxWIHSZ0n95okvp74CAAD__9jjhyA). The FAA is investigating. The collision came a day after a [rare nationwide ground stop](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkLGysyAQhZ8GOxxARC0o_sYuf3tLZ4Ul2QyCgyRO3v6OeYXb7p5z5nzn57bcgCKl-3_Y0IYcloTnEbFWLMtGsFF5pRM-Gx0P2NHllLdPWJRQhkvJpVnAVXrjoqHxdtAjiLVBK4dJj8oYYZqHdehRTBq9x9D3odcaRD9JJ7sR19GNDdkrT0pppOiN7lo0_TR2PnSrH6QIPdMCPdVc2memFOInv7GEmAt5aF3emmgfte4H6_4xNTM1n-fZuvW4WK4_U_OXhan5OjE1v_aD7xEScpd34EAlUsKDP7Fyl2Mkj_xr4ZQqlgSVcoJ4CfdcKlNzU6zfT4qRDjMwLe4bUPyWqX_c8W3VbwAAAP__FAiLPA) that federal officials blamed on aging air traffic control technology.

A United Launch Alliance Vulcan rocket carrying 40 Amazon broadband satellites [failed to reach orbit](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkL2y2yAQhZ8GdXgAIaRbqEij7qZNqVkhsDdeWA9ga5SnzyivkOZU35y_X9_rNyBhvv-EFObIcc3hqBRaC2VNCAnLOx9wJqwPeAXPmdMZV6OMk1pL7VbwDT9htdDt82gnUFsXZj1-2ck4p1z3mGOctN9gsJMfbd-7wTqlNES9bRBc7zucLz-ttdNqcLa_BTd8Tf0e-20ftYqDsCrs2LjcfjPmSCd_QonEBXe4eU4dzY_WXlX0P4RZhFmO47h5Qv_kQpB3viBhlmubMAuxBxJmuVKFWbS-ZBBmiVhqk28C-XmThywL-2dosr5jDKVKzDIS3h9NQuYEdMoISFU2li8CHyQk-MNZJqwVOV88lw2bMEtX5v11IBFWNwqr7gmQ_nVv_3n7ZzZ_AwAA___AcZln) on Sunday after an anomaly about 10 minutes into its flight from Cape Canaveral. The launch was Vulcan's [first in nine months](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkLGunDAQRb8GOq-wMWYpKNLQvbQp0awZLxONbWQGyObro918wuuudKSjq_Pra_4CYkrPnxBxDDnMCa-dUQTLHAkilSNd8Iq0r7ChzynHV5hNY5zSWmk3gxc6cbZQL2Nv79A8ahx1P9i7ca5x9Tpa6HzXBRzQOxja5d61zva-11YPnXaPmsa3T2vtdNM5297QdcO9XUL7WHrdhK6yDS4kudx-Z0qBX_nEEjgXWuDmc6x5XEW2vWp_VGaqzHRd123fwOObVmb6bIV_Ns4FhHKqzMRwJL_irj7QFwhSmelgUOfBHpLymASOogrKUZKSrALTcxUFEf7mpBizoiRYEoraQZCZBNV_b13GZbuImXbXV7Z5RiD-fJVvZj5H8y8AAP__T76XDg) and its first for Amazon Leo, the retail giant's Starlink competitor. Booster nozzle problems on two earlier flights had prompted the Space Force to pause national security missions on the rocket. ULA said it doesn't yet know the cause and will [investigate with Amazon](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJykkM2K2zAURp9G3ilYsiwlCy0GGkPTpi3tQGE25ka6Sm6rnyBrbNKnL-krdP3Bxznn53k-A0XK1y-Q0IYS5ozbErE1rHMiSFTf8waPRMsN7uhKLukRZtlLzYXgQs_gGq04K-i8NWoP_aVDK8xB7aXWve5uVh7QB6eDRhz3RoiD8cMQ4OIHIww46Mg-_4QQWvSjVsMO9XjYDz4MF29EH0amevTUSt39KpRDfJQVa4ilkoedK6mL9tbafWHDC5MTk9O2bbsttPU5Mjk9nZicYnEQmZzW9-gg81rcb2w8AMWFe4y0YuWQ4E_JPNGyUMkcQsPKE3keIl1vjUMuCeKDyenj1_NnrX5I9fbhdfx2-n48vr4cT2-fTmcmp65af98oRlq0Yaq_JqD4D7X9Z-XVyr8BAAD__--8k28) before returning Vulcan to flight.

It sits on almost every emergency shelf in America, and most of it tastes like cardboard: the MRE.
When Hurricane Helene hit, Mary, 63, and her husband David, 66, were cut off for 21 days. No power. No running water. No phone signal. The roads were washed out, and David was bedridden, fighting his second battle with cancer.
Most families stuck like that end up rationing protein bars and chalky MREs. Mary didn't. On day four, she opened one of the blue packages stacked in the corner, added water, and heated it on a camping stove. Within minutes, [it was real, slow-cooked Black Angus roast beef](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJyk0L1OwzAUQOGnSbZW_knsdPCABJkoSAwgJuvavm4vsuPIMa3K06PyCuxH33A-jvYIlGg5vUBGE0u0C163hK1htZkgU_1ernDLtJ1hRV-Wkm_RCibUjvMdVxZ8owvaAfpg9DABcz0arg_DJJRiqj8bFEzKaWToOQY9ci_dpJ12IxyYA_Q9mbvHOVecjWqQe1TjYZIhShc0Z3HsBoaBWqn7r0JLTLdywRpTqRRg70vukzm3tm6dfOjE3Ik5VsQfDJUwrJUy1gJbc4jxXt8TOVeMnXycnz9f35_e-mrCeqWUaFO6G9gpA6U_uf1zysWI3wAAAP__iHZ3XA). When David tasted that first bite, his eyes opened a little wider.
Most people assume freeze-dried meat only comes diced or crumbled. It doesn't. [Fully cooked, hand-trimmed USDA Prime roast beef](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJyk0L1OwzAUQOGnSbZW_knsdPCABJkoSAwgJuvavm4vsuPIMa3K06PyCuxH33A-jvYIlGg5vUBGE0u0C163hK1htZkgU_1ernDLtJ1hRV-Wkm_RCibUjvMdVxZ8owvaAfpg9DABcz0arg_DJJRiqj8bFEzKaWToOQY9ci_dpJ12IxyYA_Q9mbvHOVecjWqQe1TjYZIhShc0Z3HsBoaBWqn7r0JLTLdywRpTqRRg70vukzm3tm6dfOjE3Ik5VsQfDJUwrJUy1gJbc4jxXt8TOVeMnXycnz9f35_e-mrCeqWUaFO6G9gpA6U_uf1zysWI3wAAAP__iHZ3XA) can keep 97% of its nutrients and 99% of its taste for 25+ years, with no fridge and no power.
So why do mostly billionaires and the military bet their lives on it? Few people know it exists, and fewer still know you can eat it straight from the bag.
**[See what Mary had stacked in the corner (and how it's prepared)](https://email.editor.joinflyoverflorida.com/c/eJyk0L1OwzAUQOGnSbZW_knsdPCABJkoSAwgJuvavm4vsuPIMa3K06PyCuxH33A-jvYIlGg5vUBGE0u0C163hK1htZkgU_1ernDLtJ1hRV-Wkm_RCibUjvMdVxZ8owvaAfpg9DABcz0arg_DJJRiqj8bFEzKaWToOQY9ci_dpJ12IxyYA_Q9mbvHOVecjWqQe1TjYZIhShc0Z3HsBoaBWqn7r0JLTLdywRpTqRRg70vukzm3tm6dfOjE3Ik5VsQfDJUwrJUy1gJbc4jxXt8TOVeMnXycnz9f35_e-mrCeqWUaFO6G9gpA6U_uf1zysWI3wAAAP__iHZ3XA)**

| Friend —

Here’s the truth: We’re running on empty.

While we are still waiting for every vote to be counted, we are starting to run out of resources.

I am so grateful to have had your support throughout this campaign. Seriously.

We started with $0 in our bank account, and we built this movement from the ground up without a dime from the greedy corporations hurting all of us. And we spent almost everything we had to win – _and we will_.

So we need your help again to keep us afloat while we fight to count every vote and power through until this race is certified. We can’t afford to fall short when Donald Trump and the entire DC establishment are working to overturn the results of our election and undo the will of Alaskans if I win.

I am so proud that this campaign is fueled by working people. But that does mean we have to keep asking for your support until this race is officially over.

I wouldn’t ask if it wasn’t so important. So please, friend:

It sits on almost every emergency shelf in America, and most of it tastes like cardboard: the MRE.
When Hurricane Helene hit, Mary, 63, and her husband David, 66, were cut off for 21 days. No power. No running water. No phone signal. The roads were washed out, and David was bedridden, fighting his second battle with cancer.
Most families stuck like that end up rationing protein bars and chalky MREs. Mary didn't. On day four, she opened one of the blue packages stacked in the corner, added water, and heated it on a camping stove. Within minutes, [it was real, slow-cooked Black Angus roast beef](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJyk0MFq6zAQheGnsXcJHkkZyQstLtx61bTQRUtXRpbGiUC2xFhNSJ--uK_Q_c_H4Xycx7OLKa6XF7eQnVc_rnTfEtVKPF44f61hq7kw-XwjfhSON1dpFJ3AA8ABcCyct0K-jtAGq7XEPrRkQffKCC0Mtlcr0XTgg8GgCCaA-STghMIj6sn3vW6j3UEAQIDOdKejNKZHJadOoULlqVEdhVgzH-f02JesmevVO84pru7o89Ime621bI3814ihEcPMRN8UOFIoHBfi7LY6Ec17vSdyYJob-X94_nx9f3pr2YZyjynFDXWjusviYvqV619_uVnxEwAA__-l7Hge). Most people assume freeze-dried meat only comes diced or crumbled. It doesn't. [Fully cooked, hand-trimmed USDA Prime roast beef](https://email.editor.flyovernorthcarolina.com/c/eJyk0MFq6zAQheGnsXcJHkkZyQstLtx61bTQRUtXRpbGiUC2xFhNSJ--uK_Q_c_H4Xycx7OLKa6XF7eQnVc_rnTfEtVKPF44f61hq7kw-XwjfhSON1dpFJ3AA8ABcCyct0K-jtAGq7XEPrRkQffKCC0Mtlcr0XTgg8GgCCaA-STghMIj6sn3vW6j3UEAQIDOdKejNKZHJadOoULlqVEdhVgzH-f02JesmevVO84pru7o89Ime621bI3814ihEcPMRN8UOFIoHBfi7LY6Ec17vSdyYJob-X94_nx9f3pr2YZyjynFDXWjusviYvqV619_uVnxEwAA__-l7Hge) can keep 97% of its nutrients and 99% of its taste for 25+ years, with no fridge and no power.

State Grants Expand Coastal Beach Access North Carolina’s Department of Environmental Quality awarded to 10 coastal communities to build boardwalks, kayak launches, and new public access to the state’s beaches and waterways. Craven County, Emerald Isle, Newport, and Winfall round out the list. It sits on almost every emergency shelf in America, and most of it tastes like cardboard: the MRE.
When Hurricane Helene hit, Mary, 63, and her husband David, 66, were cut off for 21 days. No power. No running water. No phone signal. The roads were washed out, and David was bedridden, fighting his second battle with cancer.
Most families stuck like that end up rationing protein bars and chalky MREs. Mary didn't. On day four, she opened one of the blue packages stacked in the corner, added water, and heated it on a camping stove. Within minutes, [it was real, slow-cooked Black Angus roast beef](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFu6zAMheGnsbcEoqTY8aDhAreemhbo0KKToYSUI0COBIp10Dx94b5Ch7P9-IbzcZpOPqZ4m1_8Qk7mMN3oXhOJEE8ls1SmdSX8Ko-ca4hcZY48aaW7HcAOuqlwroUuMkGLzigksMeWHPSDPereDqq9OuMPBwTqSBEOqIw1iGdvL6YLdFShb6PbRADYBnrYe7BGgQ_YgdLBYmMVYZTMe7nSTJnn6EP6zivx_pKXNrmrSKmN-dfosdFjYKIHIUfCwnEhzr7KmShs9ZaYkSk05v_4_Pn6_vTWssNyjynF2vWNVfPiY_qV5a-vrE7_BAAA__8hPXj0). When David tasted that first bite, his eyes opened a little wider.
Most people assume freeze-dried meat only comes diced or crumbled. It doesn't. [Fully cooked, hand-trimmed USDA Prime roast beef](https://email.editor.thegeorgiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFu6zAMheGnsbcEoqTY8aDhAreemhbo0KKToYSUI0COBIp10Dx94b5Ch7P9-IbzcZpOPqZ4m1_8Qk7mMN3oXhOJEE8ls1SmdSX8Ko-ca4hcZY48aaW7HcAOuqlwroUuMkGLzigksMeWHPSDPereDqq9OuMPBwTqSBEOqIw1iGdvL6YLdFShb6PbRADYBnrYe7BGgQ_YgdLBYmMVYZTMe7nSTJnn6EP6zivx_pKXNrmrSKmN-dfosdFjYKIHIUfCwnEhzr7KmShs9ZaYkSk05v_4_Pn6_vTWssNyjynF2vWNVfPiY_qV5a-vrE7_BAAA__8hPXj0) can keep 97% of its nutrients and 99% of its taste for 25+ years, with no fridge and no power.
So why do mostly billionaires and the military bet their lives on it? Few people know it exists, and fewer still know you can eat it straight from the bag.

## Virginia Airport Chaos Calms
Northern Virginia’s [_major airports_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkT2u2zAMgE9jbwwsxj_y4KGLt9e1o8FYlC08RQokxkJuX6jtDToQJEB-BD7y19f2Rc67cPykJy9y2S1wyZ5FOG3k0ism2U-KObOI5ywnhe-8YYcjKAVq3GgXd_HWU2sWSz3T3PKiprnXOA390J6LQpyH_YGaB92NvUacO30nVmznacK5dUvdp5SqgahuRg_q_ui4UpaHqek7Nk5iusnJl0uHC46s_8SL022Pz9Yvp8grN_cfDa4NrqWUW3lnmmu3wZWSuN1zg2vVq4nExQAlJm8aXJ8xC1jvjlMyPGj_hhhAUi1IwLy95wwEhj5AVjjBX744w3Ck-A4GssQX1It5CgyP4v7NkIfEdFBocB0HUNO-D3ogYLr30FM_gdaGwE7dPOlRWa1VmxbzKs57l8fqfjzJ-T-e8p8vuhb8HQAA__9O0acc) continued to recover on Sunday from Friday’s nationwide ground stop. Dulles International and Reagan National reported only residual delays and a handful of cancellations by Sunday afternoon. Officials expected full schedule recovery by evening as airlines repositioned crews and aircraft. At Richmond International Airport, [_about 80 flights_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL2unDAQhZ_GdEbYy89SuEhDt2lTosEewyjGRvYsaPP0EVf3DW4xUx2d8-n785pfQIHi-ht2NHz6OeJVAjJjnoHykTLbDVIpyByw8Abxb5l1o3uplFT9DJbpxLmFyhkPLcJYoVHD2D710LVdtZlxQdfBMPoGXaPs0qODplVL7_VjGTxWZO4-pdR9WqvaPTv1WBrs7KI9doNoG3TEKde84Ul5pUjgwyedmGub9iqYjfko4vFL6Eno6bquWukUP-mdCzm8Q0JP94zQk1L3a4We1pze0cnC6ZAWosVQpEv_MBbpA60bF5nJbnuKTlJkzBGYUoQgv90IPVXZuOOiEKj0N-m6A4UvKv6h0NPo_wEAAP__5WSNuw) were canceled Friday and Saturday, including 30% of Saturday’s schedule. At Friday’s peak, more than 1,500 stranded passengers filled the concourses; by 9 p.m., that had dropped to about 300. At Norfolk International Airport,**** the ground stop halted outbound flights Friday. As of Saturday morning, seven arrivals and seven departures were canceled, with [_eight delays each way_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu3CAURL8Gd1gLNra3oEjjbtOmtC5wsVFYsOAGa_8-8tP7g1dMMRppdGb-vLYXhBjS_hveqKn5LeFVIxJh2SCUMxeyB-RakShipQPS37rJh5y4EFxMG1gKDbcROqc9jAjPDrWYn-MiZzWq7tDGgILRCDPM1nvj5PxcZqcmVGaZhgG7oO8-IcQtKUXvFiUG80BljfSoZjY-0AXKpacDWyh7SAF8_OSGpbf53UV9EJ2VDb-YXJlcr-vqL2ifO2RyvTcxucZsIfJvQwUaRiyVJ2hhB0Kei-cWksUIFHKqHJLjDiN8KgdPWPhe8r_keKV8Mrl2RbvzCjGGOt2M-xtC_OKhH17ZtPwfAAD__6CgjSs). At Roanoke-Blacksburg Regional Airport, some [_flights remained canceled_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkLGunDAQRb_GdF6tB3t5W7hIQ7dpU6IBDzBZYyN7FpS_j4jyB6-Yaa50dO799RpeyJHT8hM38nLMQ6KzRhKhMiCXPReZVsy1kkikKiumdx3gDg9tjDaPASfhgwaLTfAzWsJnQ950T_sFnbOuWT08TRdanEaDwUAXZjCOrO2cw5ns3TbsL54x5joAcwtfzrTjndw0wkyuU_ZOgSWXm6x0cFk4Mc7xTz6o3Ka8NdGvIntV7Q8FvYL-PM_bGcbf3ZUq6C--gt6Y67UK-pIx5TfpMeL0ruOnLLrQwjlh1P9r673kgwNV_dkDClU9R15WqRo3DjqhcE4nB9JLyZ8UdJW8K-ib4sN-coxcH5f5siHHf5byzYEPD38DAAD__8DTkss) after the stop lifted Friday evening. As a smaller airport, residual schedule disruptions carried into Saturday while airlines repositioned crews and aircraft.
## Spanberger Pulls VA from School Vouchers
Democrat Gov. Abigail Spanberger will [_not finish enrolling Virginia_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0b2OnTAQBeCnMd1crWf5LShuEZpo06ZEAwx4tMZG9lzIvn1EojxBiqlGOkefzs-P8YPES9h-0M69nusY-MqeVTmNJOmISWdHMWdW9ZzVUfjMI75hDdaCrUeaVU4eSyqWfqWSqSu4t01XtthUZVW4vsVp7uq5s1S1aOuKG-yIaLJrMzG3tpD-zrPW3odoH0tb2ffpjat5wpWrxpRvvIjG9FDHp6RNgtDqv-LJ6THHvfC9Uz2yeX8aHAwO13U99hzun8GBA7yyweGmGRyiOk4GB0kZ_koh8cnkM3zFV9g-JUDgkxOsEiQ7XuBfJ2Q442t2nIBDit7vHBQoLJAPChOnjRNcMYDCHPfDszKIGhwowfOJ7vj263uR-uW4xHvJ9S3bdhL_R6H_OcDZ4-8AAAD__-iioGM) in a new federal [_school-choice tax-credit program_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFurTAMxvGngS3oJBAODBnuwnbu2hEZY8BqSFBiQfv2FV2qzh28_WX99L29xhew57D-h52cnMsY6MqeRCiNwOmISXCDmDOJeMqyQXjPo3mYVmmtdDsCCp80NlDOboGGoC_J6WffdOZpG1tuzna1QcB2wq7vce6mSffWdoA1AurFluzuf1rr-4zR1dxZXU8PsjiZheyzaB40s8RUyUYnp5UDw-I_40mpwriX3m0iRy7qf4UZCjNc11VxytUaz8IM692FnYIoCsLClAszLDRTAq-ygJDyEcGrn_JXgVv0kPLGhxL4UJhujVqyYJncfFzsPef2Zq47sP8myR_XPJ35CgAA___IQI89), reversing a move by her Republican predecessor, Glenn Youngkin. A recent IRS letter showed Youngkin’s administration never completed the paperwork, leaving the final step to his successor, but her office said the program would not benefit public-school students. Virginia had been the first state to opt in. [_Youngkin had championed_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2upDAMBeCngS6jxEP4KSi2obvbbok8wRBrQ4ISD1fz9qustE-whbvPR_b59bV-IQeOx088aZZ7XyN9l0AilFfkfKUszmMqhUQCFfEYf5cVNPTKGGX6FZ3wTWuH7Tbv2BFOLc1mmLoRBtvZ1s96mzSNvR2GnuyTpnGDTo8auu5pDW57y3PNM8bUATCPbbTm-dJk3Qt2skPTadpYUn6Ip5vzwZFxD590U364dLZh9iJXaZ4_GlgaWP6Zk7J75081DSygwTaw6KmBxZjKUB01I6asCn6Kou3tUDhFDMr5xI4UOlH-fVD4KD5rHRhFpetKkaKUuqa4iixFXe9XYKeK8ymF0sDS5nm7vjkELn394jiRw9-L5T_Lvmf4EwAA__95_pco) the tax-credit scholarship program, which funds private school tuition, as a win for families, calling it “hugely” important. Critics, including the Virginia Education Association, warned it could divert money from public schools. The Chesapeake Education Association [_estimated potential losses_](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkbGupDAMRb8GOo8mAQamoNiG7m27JTKJmVgTMEoM6P39itlq61dYOtaVrnR0_3yNX8iR19dvXKjXYx5XOnMkVUojctokqQsoOZNqpKwB13ce7d0-wBgwjxGd8kFjjaXvZ6wJnyX1pn3WnW2builDT-3U3pv22XWtqx5PnCqqHM4OW7SdmbHk_uozxlxnrbn5rjHVdKfGTXampi3qO3lWSTcNdHB68co4x285KN2cLGXsg-qWi-pXYYfCDud53k59f8LCDpdTYQdeQQOBk2XZV9bvwg4uUMaN8E3_PUB-d6gsK2DO4vgfb3sOlCG7IBJhEkweVEC2TTLBTJ4SRjhkd4ESbEleCRfQgApO9ujBSVbwnDWxU7AWFo6RZS1T77fz4vy4bF8LcvyY6Q9HOXr7NwAA___r-qlg) of $22 million a year locally and nearly $1 billion statewide. Supporters, including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, criticized the reversal. The program takes effect Jan. 1, 2027. Spanberger has until Feb. 15 to change her mind.
## VA Restaurants Offer Thanksgiving To-Go

It sits on almost every emergency shelf in America, and most of it tastes like cardboard: the MRE.
When Hurricane Helene hit, Mary, 63, and her husband David, 66, were cut off for 21 days. No power. No running water. No phone signal. The roads were washed out, and David was bedridden, fighting his second battle with cancer.
Most families stuck like that end up rationing protein bars and chalky MREs. Mary didn't. On day four, she opened one of the blue packages stacked in the corner, added water, and heated it on a camping stove. Within minutes, [it was real, slow-cooked Black Angus roast beef](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL1q5DAUhZ_G7mawJMueKVQs7LraSSBFQipzbR2NL5F_kC4ekqcPziukON3Hd-B7u_U34sjL_YlmONlDv-CRI0SQeuK0rUnGidacIRKRZaLlI_e60s1JqZNqehqFd_Q1ld4FqkHXEk611_qiW1vbcnKDDsrQxYQWow5V61VtB9MCja00Dapkd_iUUse0Vmd_scoMFew46ADbFnUFz7Kms0zYOd15YQrxc92RzuM6l9FNIlsuzJ9Cd4XuQgK-4BPDb4lnpJWyDEA46AMxXUIozN_u__vz67-XMjm_PThGzs3xdp-J449Zfhlld_o7AAD__xY7d-w). When David tasted that first bite, his eyes opened a little wider.
Most people assume freeze-dried meat only comes diced or crumbled. It doesn't. [Fully cooked, hand-trimmed USDA Prime roast beef](https://email.editor.thevirginiaflyover.com/c/eJykkL1q5DAUhZ_G7mawJMueKVQs7LraSSBFQipzbR2NL5F_kC4ekqcPziukON3Hd-B7u_U34sjL_YlmONlDv-CRI0SQeuK0rUnGidacIRKRZaLlI_e60s1JqZNqehqFd_Q1ld4FqkHXEk611_qiW1vbcnKDDsrQxYQWow5V61VtB9MCja00Dapkd_iUUse0Vmd_scoMFew46ADbFnUFz7Kms0zYOd15YQrxc92RzuM6l9FNIlsuzJ9Cd4XuQgK-4BPDb4lnpJWyDEA46AMxXUIozN_u__vz67-XMjm_PThGzs3xdp-J449Zfhlld_o7AAD__xY7d-w) can keep 97% of its nutrients and 99% of its taste for 25+ years, with no fridge and no power.
So why do mostly billionaires and the military bet their lives on it? Few people know it exists, and fewer still know you can eat it straight from the bag.

body:
In the wake of the election results, today is a good day to remember why we are here.

| | | [](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckUHO1DAMhU-T7jqqk7SZLrpAlAoWPwghYBl5Ek8baJOocYfro8LAAf6FJevpk5_t9_3FvmBYQ5w_4kaDewS7F8sLFcafVH4chefES5gX2q1sZFcD1NBZdBweZDVWfnC-U7KiAUyvr9IYMNUy9LfW93d9h5sH7Kg1reuVI4OgW3XDpgrDOQ4AzmpBX7rG3wyB1_fem7ZrhW6O7JGpXFyKhfYHnp4hxnR2KV5c2qp1WJhzEeqNkJOQE_r7SjOul7TPQk7lyDntLOTkU0SmekN2y4mqqaRjd-SSJ6FGgEbD1TR2v7aNkN3Bm_0LCDVGfCob-XBsQo20YVifosMtY5ijUGNOhWtayZ371Zgz4X8qRabIQo3vP3398s5-NvXbbx_qf0-o9sHnX2FdQ-mM0M18Gvy5kF-TymOQvwMAAP__ygmcjg)

| | [Meeting the Moment ... Together](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckUHO1DAMhU-T7jqqk7SZLrpAlAoWPwghYBl5Ek8baJOocYfro8LAAf6FJevpk5_t9_3FvmBYQ5w_4kaDewS7F8sLFcafVH4chefES5gX2q1sZFcD1NBZdBweZDVWfnC-U7KiAUyvr9IYMNUy9LfW93d9h5sH7Kg1reuVI4OgW3XDpgrDOQ4AzmpBX7rG3wyB1_fem7ZrhW6O7JGpXFyKhfYHnp4hxnR2KV5c2qp1WJhzEeqNkJOQE_r7SjOul7TPQk7lyDntLOTkU0SmekN2y4mqqaRjd-SSJ6FGgEbD1TR2v7aNkN3Bm_0LCDVGfCob-XBsQo20YVifosMtY5ijUGNOhWtayZ371Zgz4X8qRabIQo3vP3398s5-NvXbbx_qf0-o9sHnX2FdQ-mM0M18Gvy5kF-TymOQvwMAAP__ygmcjg) Dear Friend, In the wake of the election results, today is a good day to remember why we are here. First, the ultimate battle isn’t about politics or parties. It’s about truth, and the freedom to speak it. ADF exists to remove the obstacles between people and the Gospel. We protect the first freedoms that keep the door open so that all might be free. With God’s grace, we do that regardless of which party is in power. Second, we play the long game. The terrain changes, but the strategy does not. We anticipated this shift, though we hoped it wouldn’t be this big, and that is why—with your partnership—we have pressed so hard in the courts these past few years. We will likely see more hostility toward truth in the days ahead. But we also expect new opportunities to set precedents, especially in states with leaders hostile to human flourishing. Losses at the ballot box in Nevada and Virginia, where voters enshrined a right to abortion in their state constitutions, signal what kinds of policies might soon be attempted elsewhere. We will continue to contend for the sanctity of every woman’s life and that of her unborn child. But truth won on Tuesday, too. It can never be erased, only rediscovered or rejected. And in several states, voters rediscovered the truth that men and women are different. Biology isn’t red or blue. Building on our major victory at the U.S. Supreme Court this year, voters in Arizona and Nebraska approved measures to protect girls’ sports. Arizona’s extended those protections to women’s private spaces. Nebraska’s wrote its women’s sports law into the state constitution. You might expect that from Nebraska or even Arizona. Then came Colorado and Washington. In Colorado, two measures are leading: one protecting girls’ sports, the other protecting children from dangerous transition surgeries. In my home state of Washington, voters appear to have approved a measure protecting girls’ sports. Voters are responding to the stories of girls who paid the price. In Puyallup, Washington, then-15-year-old wrestler Kallie Keeler was sexually assaulted by a male competitor whom state and school policy allowed to compete against her. The state told her it could happen again. Her emergency petition is pending before the U.S. Supreme Court. And in Camas, Washington, a male athlete who switched to the girls’ cross-country team midyear took the final qualifying spot from a deserving young woman from Puyallup High School. He will compete in the women’s state finals this Saturday. I don’t want you to miss this, friend. In 2014, when ADF took on the lie of gender ideology to uphold biological reality, few were with us. Public opinion was at best mixed. This week, the American people crossed political and ideological lines to say otherwise. This tells us the American people aren’t ready to abandon truth. Getting here took hard work, alliance-building, and persuasion. Tragically, it also took many young women paying the cost of a lie. If working at ADF has shown me anything, it is that sometimes you have to lose before you can win. But truth always defeats darkness, and lies have a way of producing harms that become impossible to deny. We are not afraid. We walk into the wind, because that is where God has called us. This is not a time for despair. Hebrews 6:18-19 reminds us it is impossible for God to lie, and it calls the hope we have in Him “a sure and steadfast anchor of the soul.” That hope is why the Lord has called ADF to keep the door open for the Gospel. You and I contend for His truth so that all might be free to find that hope and spend eternity with Him. The terrain has changed. The calling has not. Let’s go. | | [DOUBLE MY GIFT](https://email.updates.conservativeinnovation.com/c/eJyckUHO1DAMhU-T7jqqk7SZLrpAlAoWPwghYBl5Ek8baJOocYfro8LAAf6FJevpk5_t9_3FvmBYQ5w_4kaDewS7F8sLFcafVH4chefES5gX2q1sZFcD1NBZdBweZDVWfnC-U7KiAUyvr9IYMNUy9LfW93d9h5sH7Kg1reuVI4OgW3XDpgrDOQ4AzmpBX7rG3wyB1_fem7ZrhW6O7JGpXFyKhfYHnp4hxnR2KV5c2qp1WJhzEeqNkJOQE_r7SjOul7TPQk7lyDntLOTkU0SmekN2y4mqqaRjd-SSJ6FGgEbD1TR2v7aNkN3Bm_0LCDVGfCob-XBsQo20YVifosMtY5ijUGNOhWtayZ371Zgz4X8qRabIQo3vP3398s5-NvXbbx_qf0-o9sHnX2FdQ-mM0M18Gvy5kF-TymOQvwMAAP__ygmcjg)

It sits on almost every emergency shelf in America, and most of it tastes like cardboard: the MRE.
When Hurricane Helene hit, Mary, 63, and her husband David, 66, were cut off for 21 days. No power. No running water. No phone signal. The roads were washed out, and David was bedridden, fighting his second battle with cancer.
Most families stuck like that end up rationing protein bars and chalky MREs. Mary didn't. On day four, she opened one of the blue packages stacked in the corner, added water, and heated it on a camping stove. Within minutes, [it was real, slow-cooked Black Angus roast beef](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFO6zAUxvGnSbZWtpMm9eDhSpdMFCQGEJPl2se1hdNjHZ-2gqdHhUdg-La_fsP3drAHl0s-n57cCoYxRXuGWyvADGRPhJdzaIw1ulLwwoT-I7lSrBJq2ki5kZOthK2CZyv7YEYYZNQ9GDnrca_meZZ9MrMfo9PKD-BF0D5qp3UQxx1Mcb_zw77P5g5KKX8nttEpLYUTzoOGnffdKCBkRtpyAkwZY_nEK9DW49oXk5hr64Z_nVo6tUQC-IJAGUKlvAKha3wEiPf6ngwLQeyG_8vj-_Prw0tPJtRbLiW3ae5GcVpdLj8y__mSq1HfAQAA__-h5nik). When David tasted that first bite, his eyes opened a little wider.
Most people assume freeze-dried meat only comes diced or crumbled. It doesn't. [Fully cooked, hand-trimmed USDA Prime roast beef](https://email.editor.theohioflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFO6zAUxvGnSbZWtpMm9eDhSpdMFCQGEJPl2se1hdNjHZ-2gqdHhUdg-La_fsP3drAHl0s-n57cCoYxRXuGWyvADGRPhJdzaIw1ulLwwoT-I7lSrBJq2ki5kZOthK2CZyv7YEYYZNQ9GDnrca_meZZ9MrMfo9PKD-BF0D5qp3UQxx1Mcb_zw77P5g5KKX8nttEpLYUTzoOGnffdKCBkRtpyAkwZY_nEK9DW49oXk5hr64Z_nVo6tUQC-IJAGUKlvAKha3wEiPf6ngwLQeyG_8vj-_Prw0tPJtRbLiW3ae5GcVpdLj8y__mSq1HfAQAA__-h5nik) can keep 97% of its nutrients and 99% of its taste for 25+ years, with no fridge and no power.
So why do mostly billionaires and the military bet their lives on it? Few people know it exists, and fewer still know you can eat it straight from the bag.

## Trump Pins FAA Ground Stop on Biden
President Trump on Sunday [broke his silence](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL1u7CAUhJ8Gd1iAfxYXFLdxt7dNaR3DYU0WgwVn18rbR04eIc00I32abz7uyx1CDOnxH3Y05POS8KwRibAsj5JfyVXKh4cY84tKtk8kD4sSauRScjkuYCm8cZGNMx5RYdegkbep10oPQjSbgVs_daB113ln5eQH7PVkJxCdHYepd00wF05KOUqptBLtNFgp7KgHvarBw8h6gS5QLu1nDok29PErv7G0Nu9NNBvRUVn3j6mZqfk8z9am1V4lU_OFZmqW8oqBqZnKaz_4WhCeldcQMVnkOXEPwBNQyOkMDvmvO7_k-Rphx8rX4DDxdqM9NsW44wwxhjreWC8eO4T4M4f-duLbqO8AAAD__4tyhqQ) on Friday's nationwide ground stop, calling the Biden administration an "FAA disaster" and urging Congress to fund a new air traffic control system "FAST!" The FAA is investigating two potential sources of the outage: a radar facility in Amarillo, Texas, and a radio communications site in [El Dorado, Arkansas](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGunDAQRb_GdF5hP_BC4SIN3UubEg32GCZrbGQPi_bvI5JPSDPNGR3de399z99AkdL6E3a0HPKc8KoRmbHMa8ln8pXzESDGfHLJ7oUcYNatNlIpqcwMjumNs2q8DYgavxq06jl2gx76tm0226MyTxh7hM6hw5u4cTDLuPhxwQAN2VunlDJK6UG3j7F3qnVm6IdF9wGM6Fr0xLk8fmdKvGGIn_zG8nB5b6LdmI8qvn4IPQk9pc-RK99I6OkWCz0pdZ9e6Oms8i4o9BQAZMknY5GU5E7eR5Q5yJSvDQtKKC9IFaokj4kpEHoJVTo4678_YMrpIo8yRFo3lm6DfJubYv1xUYxUzVN07boDxb9Z-f8Wflv9JwAA__9xmZHw), where contractor L3Harris recently installed a router. The agency said excessive network traffic, reaching 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds, disrupted communications and radar feeds. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy spent the Sunday shows pressing lawmakers for [$50 billion](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOszAQhJ_GdETeBRxTuPgbuvztlciBdXBivMhsEuXtT9w9wjVTzEgz-ubrMl58TDHf_vuVnAQeM733RCJUxlvhZ5534S34lPgphacHSfAjajQ1QA1m9JPEF41QzS4QITUVOTj3rUXbaV0tbkbqLIG21LSmu7ZNMHQ2HvvQQwO6raI76gDAAKBFfeq7CfRkbGev2AVvVKtpjsLldOeYZaGQPvyicpp4rZJbRLZdNf8UDgoHWWiJKR2ZwmHjFKfPYRef942LeImcFQ4GUdsO6jU-qL7zknfOdfC-_qWuD2yFg18PrYqbt3dMKe7mrFp9W338majkb6e9HH4HAAD__5GcgQU), up from the $30 billion he asked for Thursday. House Speaker Mike Johnson said the outage does not need a separate investigation. More than 1,600 flights were canceled Sunday as airlines worked back to [full schedules](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFy8yAQBeDTSB0awAKjguJv1PlvU2oIWuxNEKuBtTW5fUbJEdLvvnnfe7stt4AZy_1_2MBzoqXA0TIwQ13ulZ5lbUx7CjnTkyvFT-AUFi21FUoJZZcQGV-wqH71CUDDpQevrtPotDNS9g8flVE2mjRKkxKoVUYHLtjJuileJVx69GecUsoqpZ2Ww2SiktE64961ScF2o4QVmerwQVj4ASl_0QvqEGnrs38w7627_Ov03On5OI7hNJTASKXQcV51et4pI2NsnZ65PrddNMxQWDQSKVRBRfxyxekVAetOlUUroebzp69-3Q_MGZu9dqO8bwHzTwH-22wvr78DAAD__4XqhNo).
## Huang Allies Plot Nvidia Comeback
Jensen Huang is weighing a return as Nvidia's CEO just days after resigning, and his allies have formed a "[war room](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2upDAMhZ8mdB4RD39TUGxDd7fdEhnigO-GJErCjHj7FfsKt3Fj6fvOOX--5i8SJ377TQePxYbZ8yc7LoXTvKVwepNLiJacC2dJYf3LxdKMNXagNehuprXIm2ddmdEyIz8rHnX_agYc2rqu9nF4La9lXUxvLfa2RtPrvmk1P6lfGhy4kvHGaa07rXHA-vFqV12v3dAOC7aWOtXUbKSE9PgO4svO1l3hzemxhqNy415KzOr5S-GkcPJXDLncL4XTDVY4aX2fVuG0nFk856xw-maf2cN-kt8ykHPCGeKZd_Eb-LcYIVgCJQMlQGKgGG877HKAoSsD2cIJdobEWTbPBu5QsO63gSHHC_iILlzMQNaSpFtbpdHEjzgnuetVU28HifvfpPxs__eI_wIAAP__COSdHA)" of tech executives to lobby the board and the White House. Elon Musk and two major investors back his return. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent wants an outside CEO instead. Meanwhile, Megaspeed, the Singapore company at the center of the scandal, said Sunday that suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang [left the company](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u3CAQRp8Gd7OC8Q924WKjyN1NkyKlxYVhTS4GC2bX2bePnFdI_UlH3zm_PtYPE2JIjx9mp5l9XhOdNRIzlfVR8jO5yvnwJsb85JLtF7E3K0ocQClQw2oshxetqnGzJ0JqG5qVnroRx17KZpsnRd0gp67tPGqt9WAmadBYPXiPWukmzBdOKTUohSPK29RbJe0w9uMn9t4MopPkAudy-51D4o18fOcXlZvNexPnjfmoor0LXAQu53ne9pquTeBCCZ5V4HJZCVwyb1QELvVZD7JMDuwWkoF6vCGG9EUOOEN6BRcMVKA_8JlrhUieISRAiT3s9DD1IHJQzfuCmgL3O258jr1ol2yDE-33b1dTOutPKkdTZnecIcZQBy06-dhNiP_O8_8lf834NwAA__8BRJZq) on Aug. 30, 2025. It denied wrongdoing and hired outside lawyers for an internal investigation. The timeline is in dispute. A short-seller report in May quoted a Megaspeed employee saying Alice Huang was "[actually still our boss](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO3CAQxvGnwR0rGGPsLSjSuLu0Ka0xjG0SDBbM-rRvH12UN7j6kz799fv1sXxgTDHvP_Ekx1tZMn22RMxUl72WVw6Ny7VhSuXFtfg_xBsuoMBKraW2C3qONy26C24jAuo7cnp8mgmmQanucGuPIQw4Gjv1pI3p7Tg9h94Y6MPaP6GL7utOa221hgnU4zl4rbydhmmFYUMrjKIQudTH7xIzH7Sld7mpPnw5u-QO5quJ_oeAWcCMqx_9ET3u5WsXMF-lsYD5pB3bRRRkw3eTmKInebww7zLRxhIUDNKX88L8lr7k8PLcZMxMNWOSVy0ryXzHEFH-9xAwg1IG9GgEzF114fqMKcVmR2HUfmJM_xr5e7K3g78BAAD___8CjbI)," and Singapore says its own probe into the company began in February 2025. Nvidia reports [quarterly earnings Tuesday](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOpDAMhJ8mdFlhE1i2oLiG7r_2SuQNBnyXTVaJAe3bn_hf4W8sWRrNNzN_vqYvkiBx_U0vHnRJU-SzBFblPK057XEumt4LhZB2zcn_Y11owho7C2Chm8irHDxBNQ8LM3JT8QD3h-uxb-u62gZHHWLz8A7uzt2fdQdN82SGpfHO-R4rGS47AOgAsMf69mg91L7r2_6J7UKdcTXPoinf_iaJuvESPungfPPpVYVhU30X0_wyOBocz_O86caRVFKkcNW5dAbH514kcikGxwtocAS4TmtwfPFK5c0820KfYimIZ7vtFFcbeFEbqKj9MGVLxcr179FvXKxE5RwpWIkHF5X1m2twrPIwv08JQUp3N65eXyThO7H-bOdjwP8BAAD__wOnk6o), its first with CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO.
## Top Test Scorer Confesses to AI Cheating
The man who posted the best score on South Korea's grueling tax accountant exam [admitted Sunday](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFygzAQRL8GOhidAFkUKtLQOW1KRpZORrHgGOls4r_PkF9I-3Zmd_Z9XeerjSlu90-7ouFA84ZHSciMeb5nem6-MO3BpkRPzuQeyMHOUkjVADSgZus4vnCG2puAKLGr0cBl7LXUgxD1YpyHfggKusFf9E2No8ZO2wG19AjeYh3NWQcACkBqKdpxcCCc0oO-ySFYVfUCfWTK7TfFjRcM6U0vzK2jtU5mYd5L1X1UcqrkdBxH-7YL0ZlWcjr_nJhy8pWcbOboEp6o0JOX5kEZbWmY9qY4ypgbtj8NdL0ArfXYLrymOhu_HzGlWNSl6sV9tTH9rfP_nL2M_A0AAP__7W-BfA) that he cheated with a hidden camera, a smartphone, and AI. Han Won-seok, 34, got 159 of 160 questions right in the first round, a result so good it set off online suspicion. He photographed the questions with a tiny camera, sent them to an AI, and [checked the answers](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL0SmzAQhJ9GdGIkmR-5UJGGzmlTMoc4gWLBMdJhnLfP2JM3SLPFFt_ufL8e4wNiivvyEzZ0HGjc8SoJmTGPS6ZznwvTESAlOjmTfyIHGI0yndRa6m4Ez_GFo65mFxAN3ip0ur831thWqWp1ejY-9KqfWttN3k49TroJCr2eZhugr6L74LTWndbGGlXfW6-V72xrJ9MG6ESjcI5Muf5NcecVQ_pDL8y1p61KbmU-irj9EGYQZriuq35SRuC4Yak91c8szFDo5PXbCzMkuKTPcUNhhn_brTAD0yEZ3hK8p3Nn2FniGzZZPGXMEuYtcpFM0q8f_L7Is3wSYpXdfFwxpVi6XjRq2SCm7z3-P6kvZ_4GAAD__y11jng) on his phone, he said in a video posted by his lawyer. He had denied everything until this week. Han also confessed to using the same setup on the country's [CPA exam](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFyqzAQgOHTiM7M7oKEKFS8hs6vTckoYmUUy8gj1jC5fca5Qvp_vuL_uM5Xn3Labv_9g53EMm987plFuM63Wl7bskt5Rp9zeUkt4c4S_UxA5oJ4QTP7IOngGZvFRWbirmGHw9hbshqgWV0XTCCwIWoexpH02AOYwDR0YAdeYpPcm0NEg0iWoB11QAjGavtJOnqjeuAlSantV0mbrBzzdzm4tqE8muxWkeeuun-KJkXTeZ7tvVT2K1efl3ejaPJVUsisaEIYu0F3tqlueZ4p57SbQfVwe_iUf0X524fD0U8AAAD__0-9cNk), which no one had caught. Police have opened an investigation. The government says AI cheaters will lose their credentials and face a five-year ban, and the president's office vowed to track down past offenders.

Read this first.** Automatic renewal makes life easier. No paperwork, no phone calls, no worrying about a lapse in coverage. But [that convenience could be costing you money](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFu8yAURp8Gb7G4YBM8MPxS5C3_2hFhuCS0YCx8nTRvX6Wv0PXTp3Ok83G1V5dyWm__XUFDsdoVn3tGImz21uqxhp3qFl3O9aBW_RdSdFZwoU4AJ1DWeUoPtNAFExEFyg4NnKdBCz1y3t2NliGAHmPUi1QLaLk4KZUc-RgnBxK6ZN44AFAAQgveT6MH7pUe9SLG6BQbOIZEtfWfNa10x5hf9YGt97V02dyJtp3Jf0zMTMw7-qNhX-qKr_eBiXlrTMw5hKBh4pPygcnZbd9OMnkBPigm1EHFFgzpKExesLiUu2bC9kw5p12d2cBv7_HXSH_r9DDiJwAA__9fKHrS). It sits on almost every emergency shelf in America, and most of it tastes like cardboard: the MRE.
When Hurricane Helene hit, Mary, 63, and her husband David, 66, were cut off for 21 days. No power. No running water. No phone signal. The roads were washed out, and David was bedridden, fighting his second battle with cancer.

## Senate Republicans Elect Minority Leader
Colorado Senate Republicans unanimously selected [Sen. Lisa Frizell](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuhDAQRL_GdJzshbO5wkUaukubEq3s9bGKwcisOF2-PuKkfEGaqZ7maebrPt2RM6-PT1zIS0jTSs89kwjVSSoelHnZMMi-lW9ayiozJZlAg22NaY2dMAgfNPXYRJ8SBLQNeeNu_dD1Rttm9kGHKzgYaOhCxKBRo7N0dTeX9KApNOzPPmOMNZ02PVwSOkjBpC5Eit0AqtcUWUq9yEyh5FIxlpRf5aB6CWVpsp9Ftl11HwpGBeMf8x7DK52QgvHUKBiNOaNXMGbesU2VfyjndqcVhdpH2dqF11JZXm0mjFQVjE31cXtyzrxbp3r9WJDz2y3_vO3w8BsAAP__JamDAQ) of Castle Rock as their new minority leader on Saturday morning. Frizell succeeds Sen. Cleave Simpson of Alamosa, whom Gov.-elect Phil Weiser [intends to nominate](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkb1u3EAMhJ9G6ngQV7IkFyrSXOe0KQVql3tisj_CLu8E5-kDxzkgvUvi-zjAYH68rW8kQdLtO0Ve1Po18VkDq3JZtdCDg8SDrNYj_-KYk-7sdTWdGQERcFzJqjx4Hah1i_fG0tjygtPrMPcDdmO7L7jNL7ihn6e5M64zkx_60WI_v8zYbfNrK8tHHiKO2Hc4mIunyXiLvreOXT-bZujYieZy0Z1tDrmQyz685weXi82xDcuuetSm_9aYa2Ou53lenl7lRMqFj_sWxFKqHx-NuT45fArwnwEc2OonyAWCVAJf5DeHAFFSLqLvEJgcF6CU8j1Z_nfXXQ5QpgiUHPzMkhS2u7uxgs0xiiozRI4bl8Zc27K445QQpI5TM3S3SBL-NtIvjvFYzJ8AAAD__2ncppA) as Colorado's commissioner of agriculture. The [new leadership team](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOnTAMhZ8GNhAxaQhDhi5st2tHZBLnEjUkKPEF9e0rKlXq_q-f5U_nnJ-v9YUhhvT-gQcZtn5NdNdIzFRWLnhRDMeJluuZf9GRE-_keYUBVCdEJ9SKlsNFq8TWGe_BomrJiGmWepRiUO1uFKCe9KzlNyXUvM0atJ9gmEmCHoTb2mAenxBCiXEQEnqPE3gr_GgduVFDIwdygXPpeSebYy7oso-_80Wlt_loo9mZz9qM3xtYGlju--7tVp8uz72B5d9XA8tD_yNdpYRMXaHzs8VgMdUOU8qfZKmLhI5K3cPZMeEjaotx5x1iDFVNjRzeB4b4NwR_cb_LwJ8AAAD__wVGh74) includes Sen. Byron Pelton as assistant minority leader, Sen. Janice Rich as whip, and Sen. Scott Bright as caucus chair. Sen. Barb Kirkmeyer stays on the budget committee. Frizell, a former Douglas County assessor, has served as assistant minority leader.
## Flight Delays Linger into Sunday
[Denver International Airport](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkb3K3DAQRZ9G7mbRn2Vt4SKNuy9tSjMrjbwismXkic2-fdgsBFKnvQcOHO6Pr_kLc8nb8h1XGjmkeaPrKMRMbeaGJ5W87hj42OtPWuvGT0o8a6kdKAXKzRg4nzRb7OKYkg7oOhrVcLfeWCVd9xwNBnK-t0663hovHUrrg3KDwrt0FLs8vn1KKaeMVFbfEg46BZVMiBSN18JKiplru_GTQi21YaypvOpJ7Rbq2pXxybwfwnwTehJ6uq7rdn-XvKnQEzbOoZDQ06dJ6CnSdlKDvDG1DTnXDQtgbntt_A_-u0Kkgq8DHrgsuBCsdBwQ8QWYmBp8JFeOBEurv7YIB9dd6Gkw4MmYYGUP_SNosBgDeD8kiDH1fe8f0iTXtTHuVy4lH24QVi4r5vKnjv_zmHPUvwMAAP__6nak_g) (DIA) was still tracking 316 delayed flights Sunday, two days after a nationwide FAA ground stop halted U.S. passenger flights. DIA had over 100 cancellations by 2 p.m. Sunday, according to [FlightAware data](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFugzAQgOGnMVsQPjsmGTxUalmqZO2IrvY5WD0wMidQ3r5KX6H7r2_4v27jDTPn5XHHmbyENC50bEwiVEepuBPnecUg21p-aC6LTJRkhA7cSeuTdiMGyTuNFpvoU4KAriGv-6u9GKs710w-OO1cAKdD7Fzq45XOxkLEmIwx32fbZP_ytNZOm05baBP2kIJOJkSK5gLKdhSzlNrKRKFwqRhL4mfZqbahzA37SWTdlHlTMCgYjuNoE-fHJHhgpVejYOC8k4Ih4BKImaKCQUrEp4Lh8_3j3lQf1yMz5831ynaPGTP_8fLPM7uH3wAAAP__OyR5ag). On Friday, 497 flights were canceled and 605 were delayed at the airport. Stranded travelers [found nearby hotels](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOpDAQRL8GMiNsPAYCB5eQzaUXoh67DdY1GNk9oPn71ezOH2xYKumpXv27z3eIFPflL2xo2YV5x6sQMmOeOcOJFLcDHJcj_cct7bxi4Fm1yggphTQzOI4nzhpqb0NQDkyNVvajHjotW1OvdtSoDejbw0hU2HZu7P1t6NSIgw6tUXW0b56U0siulVo1AXoVnAyd8-i7QVW6RR855YZXdIlSBp8CvdKJuXFpq8muzEepuj-Vmio1XdfVeNxPzP27r9T01qrURMkBiU_4mIkURAAQS07P3YvC6RCFI5F4YNwXEZBYxF38AEUBfmYPrzpbf1yRKBbTV7pdNoj0vYZ_eeRp1VcAAAD__ykMi0M) sold out as rates jumped from about $100 to as much as $500 a night, and some slept at the airport or in their cars. The FAA blamed Friday's shutdown on legacy equipment that became unstable when data flooded its telecommunications infrastructure. Air traffic resumed that evening.
## Pagosa Springs Museum To Be Demolished
Demolition of the Pagosa Springs History Museum is [tentatively set for today](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkDHO4yAUhE-DOyzABMcFxTbusu2WFoFHjBb8LHixlduvvFJO8Lcz-kYz8-exPFzKaXv9dgUs-bhscLYMRFAXqu6AnMruPLUd_0LBjVaItCihDJeSS7M4T-mARbsu2BiVd6YDK8dJ3wcthelWO96i0NFH-VRu9JO4eRG0kZMfw_QctOmSvfKklEYOQmrVRzeq6GUcfIAw3BXTAkIirD2t4DFjdQFj_uABtfdYumxXor2x4RdTM1PzeZ69f7Zry-UzNX8ppuZLZWre3Qub42tqhPXDy7vBu_AABXOihBtv-Kb1hEb8C_OYEcMFd9WG_Uw5p2ZGpsWruJT_V6EfvnhY9S8AAP__tvWLkw) after floods in southwest Colorado washed out the ground beneath part of the building. Board President David Hamilton said crews saved a large share of the artifacts, though a room of ranching and farming equipment was lost. The museum hopes to rebuild. The San Juan River in Pagosa Springs [peaked at 16.8 feet](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkDFvxCAUg38N2RLxgHLJwNAl23XtGHHwuKCSEMFrUP99lUqVune19dmy3-_L3cYU9-eb3dCQC8uOrSYkwrJQsSemuB3WUT3yB255pxUDLYIL3QP0oBfrKJ64KNt5E4JwVndo4DapUSrgulsNgrcwanx4zvlkQ3jhUslRyingOGnsornyAECD5KDEEOxNBAdBOo9ejoIpjj5SLgOt6HLKxfoc0lc-sQwub10yK9FRmXxlYmZibq0N7lGvLZfPxPxLMTFfKhPzGivlEl0fUs4-7s--5k9aG1bCsvd_gK4Yf7SYUqz6xhR_bjamn17652WnEd8BAAD__2ZchCg) early this month, more than a foot above the prior flood's peak, in what residents called the worst of three historic floods. The Pagosa Springs Chamber of Commerce is [matching volunteers with neighbors](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJykkUHOnSAURleDM17gwkMdOOjE2d9phwYvFyVFMMDTdPeNTbuCTs-XnOTk-_G1fNkQQ9q-24Omhn5JdNdIrVFZWrEXxXCcFls98086cmo7-baAAMOl5NIsFlu4aNG2c5P3gNZ0NMl-1IPSUphun5xYBemxH0fAYX0bs_aGwNthQEGE7y5Mj09KaaQSUsPL2x48Sq_QkVMDMC3IhZbLq-2EOeZiXfbxV76ovDAfXZz21s7K1DcGM4P5vu_X-JQ8K4PZlhYwEoP5gQzmmNFGBvM_Gf_LT7vlank9S0hb5bjbY6XCfczZcYxk0-fkV46f1IhK5YnCtq-5VB4ST0SOwdwrTiS9XsFzpdFxjX7goxqAD25Vb1z7nt6iK5M77xBjqKZnWmyHDfFPTfvPI64JfgcAAP__QwKfYw) who need help with flood cleanup through its new Love Pagosa app.

It sits on almost every emergency shelf in America, and most of it tastes like cardboard: the MRE.
When Hurricane Helene hit, Mary, 63, and her husband David, 66, were cut off for 21 days. No power. No running water. No phone signal. The roads were washed out, and David was bedridden, fighting his second battle with cancer.
Most families stuck like that end up rationing protein bars and chalky MREs. Mary didn't. On day four, she opened one of the blue packages stacked in the corner, added water, and heated it on a camping stove. Within minutes, [it was real, slow-cooked Black Angus roast beef](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFOwzAQgOGnSbZWPts4yeABCTJRkBhATJG5OzcWTh05p1Tw9Ki8Avuvb_jfT9MppJwu5-ewsBeM04WvW2YRrpPUsHNOyxpQtrV88VIuMnOUSSvtDgAHcFNASTtPNrTkY9QYXMseusH2xoJy7eyHziBa7Eih7sEOygwdOurvLA0ayLXJ3zwAcGAUWH2ModMRIRokJtPrxiqmJKUeZWYsudRAJebvsnM9Ylna7GeRdWvMfaPHRo-xMv8w1cS01rRwLWGTT-Z4q2-JGSvHxjyMTx8vb4-vbfW0XlPOaXNdY9V5CSn_yfLPKbvXvwEAAP__lIR3ZQ). When David tasted that first bite, his eyes opened a little wider.
Most people assume freeze-dried meat only comes diced or crumbled. It doesn't. [Fully cooked, hand-trimmed USDA Prime roast beef](https://email.editor.thecoloradoflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFOwzAQgOGnSbZWPts4yeABCTJRkBhATJG5OzcWTh05p1Tw9Ki8Avuvb_jfT9MppJwu5-ewsBeM04WvW2YRrpPUsHNOyxpQtrV88VIuMnOUSSvtDgAHcFNASTtPNrTkY9QYXMseusH2xoJy7eyHziBa7Eih7sEOygwdOurvLA0ayLXJ3zwAcGAUWH2ModMRIRokJtPrxiqmJKUeZWYsudRAJebvsnM9Ylna7GeRdWvMfaPHRo-xMv8w1cS01rRwLWGTT-Z4q2-JGSvHxjyMTx8vb4-vbfW0XlPOaXNdY9V5CSn_yfLPKbvXvwEAAP__lIR3ZQ) can keep 97% of its nutrients and 99% of its taste for 25+ years, with no fridge and no power.
So why do mostly billionaires and the military bet their lives on it? Few people know it exists, and fewer still know you can eat it straight from the bag.

Last week, I was struck and saddened by the Jensen Huang story. Anytime a major business leader succumbs to personal weaknesses and pays the price, it's a cautionary tale.
I'll say as an Asian American myself, seeing one of our most prominent figures - likely the biggest one from a commercial and technological perspective - hit the skids brings me no pleasure. I've also met several women at various political events whom I think may have been . . . Chinese spies.
I don't know Jensen and have never met him, which might surprise you. I suppose he's been busy. So I don't have any personal stake in that way.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e0d4a975-ff18-4460-a546-8d3b64039a2b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But I think Nvidia is going to have a rocky time without him, which may wind up affecting us all. Jensen Huang has been the company's only CEO and defined Nvidia since he co-founded it 33 years ago. You have a company built around a leader who had 60 direct reports and turned the company into a rocketship. He was the hub. This is an outfit that has no experience without him. A new CEO will mean change and a different approach, which will be a massive adjustment. According to one survey, 76% of Nvidia employees are millionaires and almost half report being worth more than $25 million. Jensen, despite his problems, kept them in place and motivated. A lot of the senior people are going to depart over the coming weeks and months for other pursuits, commercial or otherwise.
Jensen was also the center of a web of relationships, including financing, with hundreds of founders, manufacturers and investors at other firms. Nvidia is famously the nexus of a multi-billion-dollar matrix of financing commitments and supplier deals that underpin the AI buildout. He was kingmaker, taskmaster, banker, global figurehead, and godfather of the AI boom all rolled into one person. It is impossible to overstate just how much rested on Jensen; Nvidia lost $1.8 trillion of market capitalization in the wake of this scandal. Colette Kress, Nvidia's interim CEO, will be tasked with figuring out which commitments to follow through with and which ones may not make sense. Heck, even which ones are real. All while reassuring 42,000 employees that all will be well and they should stick around.
Nvidia has stood astride the AI trade and the direction of the American economy these past couple of years. Now, there's a new decision-maker trying to make heads or tails of deals that will shape whether a $3 trillion dollar investment in AI infrastructure pays off. Uncertainty abounds.
A lot of people are making jokes about this situation, which I understand on one level. A woman friend said to me, "I knew he was no good, based on his leather jacket." Bowen Yang got the call from SNL to play him this weekend.
But I think there's a real chance that we look back at Jensen Huang stepping down as one of the signal moments in the end of this phase of the AI boom. Markets sometimes look for a reason to take a direction. And we all know what happens after a boom - something none of us would enjoy.

**Good Morning!** On this day in 1945, Davis-Monthan Air Force Base was [selected](https://email.editor.thearizonaflyover.com/c/eJyk0DtuhDAQANDTmG6Rf9hs4SIN3aZNiQY8hlEMXtkWCE4fJVfIBV7xvl7jCyjSvnzChq7CHcYdzxKxVswjLOgxXLQvK31jwRg8BtwLjpJL8xDiIcwIc6UDRw2Nd8rMT6sbdMI-da-0UrZZ3STVPIHo5r4L3dSjDwq0NrqfdOh6CQ25X08IYYTinTKtV5Zb3T9tB1zJGZnm6Kmm3NYVIdOddgjxSgfmdk5bE91a67sw9cHkwOQA94ZbylcLd6QpQ77aJR1MDnvyWJgcDsKTyUFwY41tsvPvk2KkYizTfNmA4p9b_1tyOPkTAAD__yyqdYI) as the storage site for B-29 bombers. What do you do to keep feeling young? Researchers reveal that the habits that matter most are simpler than most people expect, and almost all of them are free. * * *
Picture this...
* **Universal healthcare coverage:** Automatically covers every U.S. resident from cradle to grave, regardless of employment, income, age, or pre-existing conditions.
* **Zero point-of-care costs:** Eliminates monthly insurance premiums, deductibles, copays, coinsurance, and surprise out-of-network bills.
* **End to medical bankruptcy:** Protects households from medical debt and financial ruin triggered by major illnesses or accidents.
* **Comprehensive benefits:** Covers primary and hospital care, prescription drugs, dental, vision, hearing, mental health, reproductive care, and long-term care in one package.
* **Full freedom of choice:** Allows patients to visit any licensed doctor or hospital nationwide without narrow provider networks or referral gatekeepers.
* **Massive administrative savings:** Consolidates thousands of private plans and billing rules into one streamlined claims system, saving hundreds of billions of dollars annually in insurer and hospital overhead.
* **Lower prescription drug prices:** Uses the federal government's bulk purchasing power for over 330 million people to negotiate lower prices on medications and medical devices.
* **Progressive, ability-to-pay financing:** Replaces flat, regressive premiums with progressive taxes, lowering total healthcare costs for low- and middle-income families.
* **Better preventive care:** Removes cost barriers that cause people to skip checkups and delay treatment until conditions become costly emergencies.
* **Reduced health disparities:** Guarantees uniform benefits across all zip codes, narrowing racial, rural, and socioeconomic gaps in care.
* **End to "job lock":** Decouples health coverage from employment so workers can switch jobs, launch businesses, or take caregiving leave without risking their family's care.
* **Relief for small businesses:** Frees employers from managing complex health plans and absorbing steep annual premium hikes, leaving more room for wage growth and hiring.
* **More time for patient care:** Eliminates prior-authorization battles and insurance denials, cutting administrative burnout for doctors and nurses.
* **State and local fiscal relief:** Shifts Medicaid and public-sector employee health costs to the federal program, freeing state and municipal funds for schools and infrastructure.

That’s what we could have if Congress passed cradle to grave health coverage with Medicare for All. [**You in? Good.
