Duffy declines to apologize for Friday's nationwide ground stop. International: UAE remains major hub for gold smuggled from war zones despite new regulations. Saudi Arabia executes two men. Imran Khan details inhumane treatment, asks for urgent medical care in letter to justices. About 4.5 million people have returned to Sudan, UNHCR says. Africa CDC says the Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo is still not under control. Somaliland's intelligence agency says it briefly detained five U.S. nationals it accused of threatening national security. Ecuador's President Noboa denies the U.S. has a military base near Guayaquil. Guatemala decrees a 30-day state of emergency in its eastern provinces after lawmakers killed. Mexican journalist found dead in Guerrero. Martine Moise, widow of Haiti's assassinated president Jovenel Moise, registers as a presidential candidate. This is Drop Site Daily, our free news recap We send it Monday - Friday Iran Iran claims six-drone strike on U.S. radar system in Bahrain: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) Sunday that it launched six drones successfully targeting a U.S. air defense radar system at Bahrain's Al-Rifaa helicopter base, describing the operation as the second phase of its response to U.S. military actions in the Strait of Hormuz. Bahrain's military, however, said its air defenses intercepted and destroyed the Iranian attacks before they reached their targets. The strikes followed an earlier Iranian drone attack on Bahrain on Friday, the first targeting a Gulf country since September, when the IRGC also claimed to have destroyed a U.S. early-warning radar system. U.S. deploys third aircraft carrier to Middle East: The United States deployed a third aircraft carrier strike group to the Middle East amid heightened tensions with Iran. The USS Theodore Roosevelt entered the U.S. Central Command area of responsibility on Sunday, joining the USS George Washington and USS George H.W. Bush. Meanwhile, the European Union Aviation Safety Agency extended its warnings for airlines operating in Middle Eastern airspace until January 31, citing continued risks from the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. The advisory covers Iran, Saudi Arabia, Jordan, Lebanon, Iraq, and the wider Gulf region. Six oil tankers struck mines, caught fire in Strait of Hormuz, Iran says: Iran's IRGC Navy Monday that two more oil tankers struck naval mines overnight while attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz through a "prohibited" southern route, triggering explosions and fires. The IRGC claimed the vessels were operating under U.S. military guidance, bringing the number of tankers it claims to have sunk since Sunday to six. Iran's regular navy reported that another tanker caught fire after striking a mine east of the strait. The reports have not been independently verified. Separately, UK Maritime Trade Operations reported Monday that a tanker was struck by an unidentified projectile while transiting outbound through the Strait of Hormuz, sparking a fire in its engine room. All crew members were accounted for, while the extent of the damage and environmental impact remain unknown. IRGC claims capture of eighth intact U.S. drone in Hormuz: The IRGC Navy Monday that it forced a U.S. MQM-170 drone to land intact using electronic warfare systems in the Strait of Hormuz. The IRGC said it was the fourth MQM-170 and the eighth U.S. drone captured intact by its forces in the strait. The force also claimed to have intercepted, captured, or destroyed several other types of U.S. drones, including MQ-9s, MQ-1s, and LUCAS attack drones, since the start of the U.S.-Israeli war against Iran. Israel reportedly warns U.S. of Iranian drone plot targeting Trump; Tehran denounces "disinformation": Israel's Mossad intelligence agency provided the CIA with information suggesting Iran was planning drone attacks targeting President Donald Trump and senior administration officials, Israel Hayom reported Saturday. The newspaper said the warnings prompted heightened security in Washington, including the relocation of some officials to protected facilities and a reduction in Trump's public appearances. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said U.S. officials receive "aspirational threats from Iran" daily, adding that Washington was already aware of the threats and was prepared to respond. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei rejected the allegations, accusing Israel of orchestrating a disinformation campaign to build Western public support for escalating the war. "Fear must be manufactured to push the public into backing an escalation of the war," he said. Bahrain sentences convicts 69 defendants over alleged ties to Iran, confiscates $21.2 million: A Bahraini court on Monday 64 defendants to life imprisonment and five others to 15 years in prison over accusations of establishing a group linked to Iran's IRGC and seeking to overthrow the government, according to the Britain-based Bahrain Institute for Rights and Democracy. Bahrain's public prosecution the court also ordered the confiscation of more than $21.2 million and imposed fines of approximately $265,000 on some defendants. Palestine Israeli forces kill one Palestinian, wound five others across Gaza: A young Palestinian man was by Israeli forces in the Al-Qassasib neighborhood of Jabalia, northern Gaza, on Monday, according to WAFA. Two other Palestinians sustained gunshot wounds in the nearby town of Beit Lahia. In southern Gaza, Israeli forces shot and wounded three Palestinians, including a child, inside a school south of Khan Younis. Israeli forces detain 13 Palestinians in occupied West Bank raids: Hebron: Israeli forces 11 Palestinians, including journalist Yasser Jaradat, during a raid on Sa'ir, on Monday, according to WAFA. In nearby Al-Shuyukh, soldiers closed the town's entrance, seized vehicles, and turned homes into military posts. Schools in both towns suspended classes due to the military presence. Jenin: Israeli forces two Palestinians after raiding their homes in Jenin city. Soldiers also raided Al-Fandaqumiya, Burqin, and Rummana, firing tear gas in the latter and causing several cases of suffocation. On Sunday, an Israeli military jeep ran over two Palestinians riding a motorcycle east of Jenin, leaving one with a broken foot and the other with a head injury, according to the Palestine Red Crescent Society. Nablus: Israeli forces raided Beit Furik, east of Nablus, and Beita, south of the city. In Beit Furik, soldiers stormed several businesses, destroyed equipment in one shop, and assaulted residents, according to WAFA. In Beita, Israeli forces entered Palestinian homes and fired live ammunition and tear gas canisters. Tubas: Israeli settlers live ammunition toward Palestinian herders in northern Yarza, east of Tubas, forcing them to abandon grazing areas. Palestinian prisoners suffer severe weight loss and scabies in Israeli prison: Palestinian prisoners held at Israel's Naqab Prison are suffering deteriorating health conditions amid medical neglect, poor sanitation, and a lack of treatment, the Palestinian Commission of Detainees and Ex-Detainees Affairs reported Monday. Mustafa Abu Al-Fiya, 39, from Tulkarm, suffers from spinal disc problems and heart disease and has lost approximately 14 kilograms without receiving necessary medical care. Qais Al-Habal, 25, from west of Ramallah, has lost 39 kilograms, and suffers from severe scabies and boils. Two other prisoners from Jerusalem are also suffering from scabies. Australia, Canada, UK, and Italy urge Israel to allow 150,000 tents into Gaza amid deadly winter storms: The foreign ministers of Australia, Canada, the UK, and Italy a joint statement Monday urging Israel to immediately allow 150,000 tents and other essential supplies held at the border into Gaza, warning that the humanitarian situation is "dire" as winter storms devastate displacement camps. "The crossings must be opened, and the tents allowed in," the ministers said without threatening any repercussions or sanctions, calling for "immediate, rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access." Recent flooding has damaged or submerged tens of thousands of tents, while at least four children and a woman have been killed. Guardian: Israel uploaded millions of photos of Palestinians to Amazon 's facial recognition platform: The Israeli military uploaded 3.5 million photos to Amazon's cloud platform in order to use the company's facial recognition technology to analyze images of Palestinians, according to an by the Guardian. The vast catalogue of images was moved into Amazon's cloud in the early months of the Israeli genocide in Gaza that began in October 2023. The large set of images was moved into an Amazon data center near Tel Aviv. The Israeli military informed Amazon of the decision to upload the images in early 2024 so it could use Rekognition, Amazon's AI-powered image analysis platform. An Israeli military source told the Guardian that Amazon's cloud infrastructure was used due to the "very large scale" of images collected at checkpoints in Gaza that Palestinians were made to pass through after being forcibly displaced by the Israeli assault. Palestinian lawmaker elected deputy speaker of Israeli Knesset: Ahmed Tibi, chairman of the Joint List faction and leader of the Ta'al Party, has been elected deputy speaker of Israel's parliament, the Knesset. His appointment follows historic gains by parties representing Palestinian citizens of Israel in last month's elections, with the Joint List and United Arab List (Ra'am) securing a combined 19 seats. Yemen Ansarallah seizes over 2,000 square kilometers in southern Yemen, takes control of Bab al-Mandab front: Ansarallah over 2,000 square kilometers of the Al-Madaribah Wa Ras Al-Arah district of the Lahij governorate in a single day with its forces now controlling all of the Bab Al-Mandab front. The Ansarallah offensive in Lahij Governorate in southern Yemen effectively encircled the remaining forces loyal to the Saudi-backed Presidential Leadership Council in the Bab al-Mandab area on Sunday. Ansarallah forces reached Al-Kharaz camp at the southern foot of Jabal Kharaz in the Al-Madaribah Wa Ras Al-Arah district and established fire control over the last remaining road out of Bab al-Mandab. Saudi-backed forces said they are withdrawing from positions overlooking the strait to reinforce defenses around their interim capital, Aden. The UN Refugee Agency warned that fighting is approaching a displacement camp housing 9,600 people in Lahij governorate. Three Yemenis, including child, killed in strikes on Sana 'a and Amran: Three Yemenis, including a child, were killed and 15 others wounded in separate strikes on Ansarallah-controlled areas of Yemen on Monday, according to the Associated Press citing health authorities. A drone strike on a home in the Al-Sarar neighborhood of Sana'a killed a child and wounded seven people, while airstrikes on a privately owned fuel station in Harf Sufian district of Amran governorate killed two people and wounded eight others. Ansarallah blamed Saudi Arabia for the attacks. Ansarallah claims strikes on Riyadh airport, financial center, and Saudi oil pipeline: Ansarallah two ballistic missiles targeting King Khalid International Airport and a financial center in the Saudi capital, Riyadh, military spokesperson Yahya Saree said Sunday. Saree also claimed that two drones struck pumping stations 5 and 6 along Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline in the Riyadh region. He said both operations successfully hit their targets. The claims have not been independently verified. Ansarallah releases 600 detainees in Sana 'a, bringing unilateral releases to 2,612: Ansarallah 600 detainees in the capital, Sana'a, on Sunday, according to the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC). The organization said its delegates interviewed detainees privately before their release and provided assistance for their return home, but did not participate in selecting those freed. Abdul Qader al-Murtada, head of Ansarallah's National Committee for Prisoners' Affairs, said the latest release brought the total number of detainees unilaterally freed by the group since the war began to 2,612. Last month, the ICRC reported that Ansarallah had released another 159 detainees. Armed men approach oil tanker east of Yemen 's Socotra island: A tanker was approached by a suspicious ship and a small boat carrying four armed men approximately 430 nautical miles east of Yemen's Socotra island, the UK Maritime Trade Operations reported Monday. The tanker's captain reported seeing a ladder aboard the smaller vessel during the incident. Lebanon Israeli forces abduct two Lebanese brothers in Shebaa, strike southern Lebanon despite ceasefire: Israeli forces advanced into the outskirts of Shebaa in southern Lebanon on Monday, raided a home, and two brothers, before withdrawing, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. The Khiam Rehabilitation Center for Victims of Torture condemned the abductions, noting that a third brother, Maher, was abducted by Israeli forces in June 2025 while herding goats near the town. Elsewhere, Israeli warplanes Kfartabnit in the Nabatieh district, while intermittent artillery shelling targeted the Ain Al-Samahiyah area between Zawtar Al-Sharqiyah and Mifdoun. Two Israeli drones also exploded over the Al-Rajm area of Mifdoun within 15 minutes of each other. Israel strikes Syria-Lebanon border, claims weapons shipment destined for Hezbollah: The Israeli military Monday that it struck a weapons shipment allegedly destined for Hezbollah along the Syria-Lebanon border, accusing the Lebanese group of using areas across Lebanon for weapons smuggling and military activities. Israel said it would continue operations to "remove threats." U.S. News Van Hollen accuses Schumer of attempting to rush Senate election: Sen. Chris Van Hollen , the Maryland senator challenging Schumer for the job of majority leader, charged New York's Sen. Chuck Schumer with pushing for a "coronation," but told Politico he had the support to block any attempt to move the election to this week. Schumer's camp denied any such plan exists, emphasizing his confidence that he retains at least majority support inside the caucus and will be re-elected leader. Van Hollen** addressed his challenge to Schumer on ABC's "This Week" on Sunday, saying that he thinks he has "a very open lane" in the race, and accusing Schumer's team of spreading "misinformation" and trying to "instill fear" in senators who may back him. He argued that midterm voters rejected Trump's policies, wars, corruption, and costs but "haven't fully hired the Democrats," so "going back to business as usual and status quo" won't earn their trust. Schumer has said he has the votes to continue serving as Democratic leader. Senate permitting reform, energy bill headed for final passage: The so-called Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act is undergoing final negotiations as environmental lawyers push to add ways to challenge energy projects and tribal advocates look to tighten tribal participation provisions. The clean energy industry remains in lockstep support of the bill, as does the fossil fuel industry. U.S. loses measles elimination status: The U.S. its measles elimination status, an expert panel from the Pan American Health Organization announced last week. The organization made the widely expected decision after a three-day meeting in Washington, concluding the virus has been transmitted continuously for more than 12 months. The CDC counts 5,412 confirmed cases this year versus 2,289 in all of 2025, the highest since 1991's 9,643, with Pennsylvania's outbreak accounting for more than 1,500 cases and six deaths. These are likely undercounts. Vaccine skepticism accounts for much of this rise, with distrust in vaccines fueled by ranking officials, including Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. Canada and the UK have also lost their status over the past year. Alaska continues counting votes, with Peltola increasing her lead over Sullivan: Democrat Mary Peltola now in Alaska's Senate contest by nearly 4 points, more than 11,000 votes, after the latest batch of votes was counted and results were released on Saturday. She netted nearly 2,000 votes from the latest batch. Decision Desk HQ shows her at 49.8% with 91% counted, just shy of the majority she needs to avoid ranked-choice tabulation. Her campaign again declared victory, saying "there is no mathematical path for Sullivan to win," though no major outlet has called the race as of Monday. All votes must be reported by Nov. 18. Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins won the state's gubernatorial race, with the AP calling the race in his favor on Friday. Kreiss-Tomkins, 37, will replace Republican Mike Dunleavy , who is term-limited and has held the post since 2018. He described himself as a "man of the middle" who would work in a "bipartisan" fashion during the campaign and said he would pay special attention to "unsexy and non-glamorous" issues like wait times for state permits and government benefits like Medicaid. He will be the state's first Democratic governor since 2002. Trump 's portfolio likely held $13 million to $62 million in Nvidia stock as of August, the Washington Post finds: President Donald Trump, whose portfolio has logged tens of thousands of stock trades in his second term, between $13 and $62 million in Nvidia stock as of the end of August, according to a review of his financial disclosures from that month. The actual value range may have been higher, the Post noted, citing Nvidia's rising share price. During his second administration, Trump has given the company's leadership major concessions, allowing its former CEO Jensen Huang extraordinary access to his administration. The White House maintains that "the President does not pick or trade individual stocks" and that independent managers handle his portfolio. Nvidia reportedly donated $25 million to Trump's White House ballroom, which it says was "independent of business interests." International student enrollment falls at U.S. colleges : New international student enrollment at U.S. universities 15% this fall after an 18% drop last year, according to a survey of more than 800 universities released by The Institute of International Education on Monday. The survey shows that total international enrollment is down 9%, following a 3% drop last year. The administration's trade war with China and immigration crackdown are likely causes for this decline, as are the budget cuts at major research universities. Incoming Rep. Don Leonard backing Ayanna Pressley: Ohio's Don Leonard , who made headlines by saying that he had been threatened by senior Democrats over his reluctance to back Hakeem Jeffries for speaker, appeared on Breaking Points Monday morning and said that he was leaning toward voting for Ayanna Pressley , who has not announced a campaign but has been drawing support regardless. The leadership election is scheduled for Wednesday, and Jeffries still has no official opponent. Federal prosecutor accuses Warren of preparing "to target private individuals close to" Trump and orders her to preserve documents: U.S. Attorney for the Southern District of Texas Aaron Reitz , a former chief of staff to Sen. Ted Cruz(R-Texas), Sunday that Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), in line to chair the Senate Banking Committee, appears "eager to wield" the gavel "like a tomahawk, hunting for the scalps of President Trump's private associates," one of several barbed references made to Native Americans made in the letter, alluding to attacks made on Warren over her past claims of Native ancestry. He gave "formal notice" to preserve documents on oversight efforts, warning of "sanctions, adverse-inference instructions, or other penalties," and said he asked the same of Sens. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) and Elissa Slotkin(D-Mich.). Duffy declines to apologize for Friday 's nationwide ground stop: A router being by an FAA contractor in Arkansas overwhelmed the nation's aviation communication network, leading the agency to ground all flights on Friday. The delay stranded hundreds of thousands of travelers and caused thousands of cancellations through the weekend. Transportation SecretarySean Duffy told NBC's "Meet the Press" on Sunday that Friday's nationwide ground stop "happened on my watch," but "I can't apologize for what was passed off to us." He told the program that operations should normalize by Monday, but that he can't guarantee it won't recur until an investigation is completed. 📥 Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email DC Correspondent Julian Andreone at Julian@dropsitenews.com. Other International News UAE remains major hub for gold smuggled from war zones despite new regulations : The United Arab Emirates (UAE) remains a key trading hub for gold smuggled from war zones despite new regulations imposed on the Emirati government under international pressure, according to a new by Swissaid. At least 591 tons of such illicit gold valued at $74 billion was imported into the UAE, mostly in 2024, the report found. Much of the smuggled gold was conflict-related and smuggled out of Africa--including Guinea, Mali, and Sudan--as well as other countries including Russia and Yemen. "The UAE remains by far the main destination for gold linked to armed conflicts in Africa. And it continues to be a major destination for gold exports from countries subject to international sanctions," the report said. Switzerland was the leading importer of gold from the UAE and does not appear to be scaling back its trade with Dubai. Between January and September 2026, more than 400 tons of Emirati gold were imported into Switzerland. Saudi Arabia executes two men: Saudi Arabia executed two men, Jawad Abdullah Qureiris and Fadel Hassan al-Safwani, on Saturday, to the European Saudi Organization for Human Rights (ESOHR). One of the charges against Qureiris concerned his participation in a 2011 protest in the eastern city of Qatif calling for civil rights and the release of detainees when he was just 16 years old. Safwani, who also took part in protests in Qatif and was tried on terrorism-related charges, EOSHR said. Both men were detained in 2020 and were among 210 people executed in Saudi Arabia so far this year, according to ESOHR. Imran Khan details inhumane treatment, asks for urgent medical care in letter to justices: Pakistan's former Prime Minister Imran Khan, imprisoned for more than three years, has to the chief justices of Pakistan's three top courts detailing inhuman treatment he has received in solitary confinement and asking for urgent medical care for himself and his wife, Bushra Bibi. Khan says he has been isolated for up to 22 hours daily since December 2025, denied regular family visits and access to lawyers, books, and television. In the letter delivered through his lawyer, Khan says he has lost 85 percent of the vision in his right eye and that dangerously high blood pressure has left him at risk of brain hemorrhage or cardiac arrest. He says Bushra Bibi faces permanent blindness if she does not get urgent surgery. Khan alleges that authorities ignored a Supreme Court order requiring hospitalization. "I will only remain able to prove my innocence if I stay alive," he wrote. Khan and his wife were sent to jail on various charges by the military-backed regime more than three years ago after his government was removed with American approval in April 2022. More recently, his three sisters were also jailed in September ahead of a planned opposition march. Noreen Niazi and Uzma Khan were released November 12, after 53 days without charge, while Aleema Khan remains in jail. About 4.5 million people have returned to Sudan, UNHCR says: Since 2024, about 4.5 million Sudanese have to their home country, according to a Monday report from the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights. The returnees are 51% male and 49% female, and 72% intend to go back to their area of origin. The largest numbers came from Egypt (943,000) and South Sudan (225,000). Africa CDC says the Ebola outbreak in the DRC is still not under control: The ongoing Ebola outbreak in central and Eastern Africa is "still not under control," the Director-General of the Africa Center for Disease Control, Jean Kaseya, Reuters Sunday. "If we don't stop this outbreak now, it would be the worst Ebola outbreak that the world will have," he added. More than 11,200 cases and 5,500 deaths have been reported since May 15, with over 80% of new cases emerging outside contact lists. Only $1.3 billion of the $2.9 billion pledged by donors has been released for use, and some health workers haven't been paid for months. The recent outbreak is the second-largest and second-deadliest Ebola outbreak on record. Somaliland 's intelligence agency says it briefly detained five U.S. nationals it accused of threatening national security: Five U.S. nationals were briefly detained in the breakaway republic of Somaliland, its intelligence agency late Sunday, claiming it had monitored them since arrival and conducted a "lengthy investigation." The announcement provided no details regarding their identities or alleged actions. A source told Reuters that they work for Parallel Black, a company registered in Delaware less than two months ago, and a Nov. 4 letter seen by Reuters shows Somaliland's foreign minister invited them to conduct investment feasibility studies. The source also told the wire service those detained left the country on an Ethiopian Airlines flight Monday afternoon. Ecuador 's President Noboa denies the U.S. has a military base near Guayaquil: Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa Sunday that U.S. personnel at Taura Air Base are there only for "temporary activities" under bilateral cooperation, and that "it's not an American base. It's an Ecuadorian base." He did not address the U.S. aircraft present at the site, nor did he respond to a journalist's request to visit the base. Last month, the AFP documented at least 20 U.S. military flights there from June to mid-October, as well as the installation of dozens of tents and infrastructure work. Ecuadorian air force commander Gen. Mauricio Salazar, who asked the armed forces to clarify the deployment's legality in a September letter, was removed and reassigned. Human Rights Watch calls the U.S.-Ecuador partnership "perilous," saying both governments have committed serious rights violations by framing their fight against organized crime as a war. Guatemala declares state of emergency in its eastern provinces after lawmakers killed: Guatemalan authorities a state of emergency in the eastern provinces of Zacapa and Izabal, a week after the shooting of a lawmaker Julio Cesar Portillo in Rio Hondo, who later died, and three police officers also killed in the attack. Authorities did not say who was responsible for the shooting. Last week, the U.S. State Department designated several crime groups operating in Zacapa as terrorist organizations, accusing them of ties to Mexican cartels. Mexican journalist found dead in Guerrero: The body of Eduardo Flores, a journalist who security, social issues, and missing persons, was found on the outskirts of Acapulco on Saturday, according to his employer, Enfoque Informativo. Guerrero authorities announced an investigation into the killing on Sunday. Article 19 has documented 181 journalist killings in Mexico since 2000, including six in the first seven months of 2026, and Reporters Without Borders ranked Mexico second-most dangerous for reporters last year after Gaza, with murders of journalists rarely solved. Now, I need your help to defend our win. | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143542057/660567796/-1430343034?amount=10&refcode=LOC_EM_FR_2026.11.16_Hubbard-Split_B1_F1_S1_C1_90OP_RS-T0&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODg1OCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlMTY5ZGQ5ZS1kYWUxLWYxMTEtOTFmMC0wMDBkM2ExOGUyNDQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=sCVYEXGHMNRdpQJbUVMZ5UV51g1vA2bAaSp4DsgJ0jo=) Folks, it’s Chuck Hubbard. If we haven’t met before, I’m a native of northwestern North Carolina who's spent forty years of my career working in local journalism, and I'm also the Democrat who is currently up by 335 votes against Virginia Foxx, _**the second most-powerful Republican in the House.**_

This is the closest House race in the entire country, and it could also be one of the most important.

As Chair of the Rules Committee, Virginia Foxx directly blocked the House from voting on Trump’s tariffs and the release of the Epstein files. When Elon Musk and DOGE ransacked our federal government last year, she stood by and cheered them on. She’s made a name for herself yelling at reporters to shut up and screaming at staff for using the wrong elevator. And for twenty years, she’s stepped on the backs of working people in order to climb the ladder in Washington, DC, _**all while making millions playing the stock market.**_

Meanwhile, I spent my career reporting the truth at the local newspaper my grandfather started after WWI. I always made an effort to bring my readers just the facts without any bias. In that same spirit, my team and I are working around the clock to make sure every legal ballot in this race counts, because no matter who they voted for, all of our neighbors deserve to be heard.

**For the first time in decades, North Carolina’s Fifth District will be represented by a Democrat.** I’m ready to roll up my sleeves and get to work to lower costs and fight corruption in Washington – but Republicans are going to do all they can to ensure this doesn’t happen. **They’re going to challenge every single vote.**

Just 335 votes could end Virginia Foxx’s political career and the decades of nastiness – **but this week will be the most critical of the campaign.** I need your help now to ensure we have the resources required to defend this seat and make sure our neighbors are heard. She’s made a name for herself yelling at reporters to shut up and screaming at staff for using the wrong elevator. And for twenty years, she’s stepped on the backs of working people in order to climb the ladder in Washington, DC, all while making millions playing the stock market. Last week, Democrats won historic majorities in the House and Senate, receiving an extraordinary mandate to take on the bad actors they campaigned against: President Donald Trump, the Republican Party, data centers, and Big Tech. This week, in their first major action since then, Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer and 21 other Democratic senators voted to fast-track a Republican bill that would eviscerate America's bedrock environmental laws in order to, in [Trump's words](https://substack.com/redirect/4c956583-4581-4e24-84cb-43e594e7d4f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), "codify our America First Energy Agenda" of building "Pipelines, Mines, and Power Plants faster than ever before" so that America remains "Number One" in data center construction.
So what can explain this almost unimaginable betrayal--and can it be stopped?
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=4981170&post_id=225063257&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjI1MDYzMjU3LCJpYXQiOjE3OTQ4NDY2OTEsImV4cCI6MTc5NzQzODY5MSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTQ5ODExNzAiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.kDjb3yEYQBCI252b7UYs_0Rk2qiBkx0guYcwcFDwAx8)
The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, or BAAJA, which the Senate is [expected to vote on](https://substack.com/redirect/63a79653-ad75-4bfd-b15b-f4f453d70759?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) next week, has been framed as a compromise to make it easier to build both clean energy and fossil fuel infrastructure. It was developed behind closed doors by Senate Republicans and two Democrats, Sheldon Whitehouse and Martin Heinrich. But there was a fundamental mismatch in this secretive drafting process. The fossil fuel industry has been all in for permitting reform--indeed, it has long been the top priority of the [American Petroleum Institute](https://substack.com/redirect/b06c5d45-7aaf-4e14-bdbc-f55fd3b1a0f0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the lobbying arm and political face of major oil and gas corporations. So Big Oil was involved in BAAJA's drafting.
Whitehouse and Heinrich, by contrast, kept Democrats' traditional allies in the dark--not just environmental groups, which are uniformly opposed to the legislation, but [tribal organizations](https://substack.com/redirect/a3835ace-5b94-4716-8054-e765b50ded28?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (many of which released a joint statement condemning BAAJA provisions that "fundamentally undermine Tribal sovereignty" and "threaten sacred sites and cultural resources"); racial justice organizations like [NAACP](https://substack.com/redirect/bfdca6e0-2c9b-48af-9209-4f1abc406edb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (which warned that BAAJA "directly threatens the health, safety, and future of Black and frontline communities"); and anti-ICE groups like [Detention Watch Network](https://substack.com/redirect/ed97681d-a4d3-4361-8e7f-58751fdda45d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (which condemned how BAAJA will "pave a path for detention expansion by making immigration detention facilities easier to build and much harder to stop").
The upshot is that the staff of two Democratic senatorial offices were alone at the negotiating table, while Republicans had the full lobbying, analyzing, and bill-drafting capacity of the entire fossil fuel industry. So of course the Democrats got rolled. And BAAJA reflects this asymmetry in the severe lopsidedness of its ostensible "compromise."
The positive pitch from BAAJA's Democratic-leaning cheerleaders, like Democratic strategist Adam Jentleson's Searchlight Institute, is that the legislation will be a huge boon to Democrats' affordability and climate goals by lowering energy costs and supercharging the build-out of renewables. These claims are dubious at best. It's essentially impossible to confidently model the full climate effects of a legislative package like BAAJA, but current analyses include [predictions](https://substack.com/redirect/efdf0d7f-0826-46ab-83d8-74aa5c64e409?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) out of Purdue University that BAAJA will actually increase both "domestic energy-related greenhouse gas emissions" and "domestic mortality attributable to air pollution from fossil fuels." The most optimistic modeling, from [Rhodium Group](https://substack.com/redirect/ce521a23-c8cd-4bdc-b126-9227604179fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), predicts a range: from BAAJA having zero effect on greenhouse gas emissions to a best-case scenario of reducing U.S. emissions by a negligible 4 percent by 2040. Rhodium's modeling on affordability is similarly laughable, with a best-case scenario reduction of energy bills by $4-$7 a month by 2040.
So that's what Democrats stand to gain from supporting this Republican bill. What are they giving up? From an environmental perspective, the costs are almost unimaginable. BAAJA severely weakens the [Clean Water Act](https://substack.com/redirect/308fbfa1-aee7-4605-b25c-271229297b65?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), robbing states and tribes of their ability to protect water quality and require adequate safeguards for activities that pollute or destroy water resources. It practically nullifies the [Endangered Species Act](https://substack.com/redirect/c250969c-40bb-4878-931f-8cd58cb4d3e3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by delegating its core responsibilities to the states, most of which either oppose the act's wildlife protections or lack the expertise and resources to adequately fulfill these obligations. And it essentially repeals the [National Environmental Policy Act](https://substack.com/redirect/e079f0f2-d467-4a9b-9487-ba4ff62eb977?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the bedrock environmental law that gives the public a voice in decisions that impact the environment, by prohibiting the enforcement of NEPA violations. These three legal frameworks are responsible for most the improvements in water quality, green space, and wildlife recovery in our country over the last half-century.
And that's just the beginning. Other provisions of BAAJA go to even greater lengths to radically lock in fossil fuel development far into the future. The "disparate treatment" section of the bill effectively makes the permitting decisions of the Trump administration permanent. In the words of [David Bookbinder](https://substack.com/redirect/8bb589be-a7b9-4ec1-9f62-040a05964e09?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), an environmental lawyer who has worked for both the left-leaning Sierra Club and the libertarian Niskanen Center, "The result of making these energy permitting policies permanent is that future administrations will be unable to effectively reduce GHG emissions." BAAJA also guarantees not just the construction of fossil fuel projects but also their "operation at full capacity," permanently blocking any future administration from regulating energy infrastructure.
If you're thinking this legislative assault on the environment sounds like it was pulled straight out of Project 2025, well, [you're right](https://substack.com/redirect/17c8ec99-fb2d-4ec1-9675-c19f0a195ac6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--and the authors of Project 2025 are strong [supporters](https://substack.com/redirect/e56e3e87-a713-405a-ade2-ccd10884074a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of the bill. BAAJA is also the [top legislative priority](https://substack.com/redirect/b2fc12f3-0755-4679-b9d7-ae76e3d74f59?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of API, ExxonMobil, Chevron, Shell, BP, ConocoPhillips, and other fossil fuel giants. So no wonder climate advocates have been sounding the alarm--and not just progressive leaders like [Bill McKibben](https://substack.com/redirect/a3cd51bf-6c6b-48ff-884d-8a5ee4e4b31a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), but moderate climate advocates like [Jody Freeman](https://substack.com/redirect/295f96bd-13b2-4a13-b27e-600712b78891?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [John Podesta](https://substack.com/redirect/b64c311a-ac39-4307-95d3-10b164916759?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and [Al Gore](https://substack.com/redirect/1fdd7b8f-eb10-42c8-b5a8-2b4ff1bebd8a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), who recently warned that "now is not the time to give the Trump administration freer rein to double down on fossil fuels--which is what President Trump would surely do." This point is crucial: Trump will be implementing BAAJA if it passes, and he very clearly has no intention of allowing the "supercharge clean energy" side of the bargain to move forward. Indeed, just this week Trump [reiterated](https://substack.com/redirect/41fc5aa1-1879-4376-9a55-c33f0bd5f164?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that he is not going to approve any wind turbines, even if Democrats submit to his desire to "codify our America First Energy Agenda" by passing BAAJA.
Of course, Big Oil companies aren't the only villains that want to see this Republican legislation pass. Big Tech is also all in, from [Marc Andreessen's](https://substack.com/redirect/c1a9bfc8-8153-4ddd-8c36-16d25283d467?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) tech venture firm to ITI, the trade association for OpenAI, Nvidia, Meta, Amazon, Google, and other tech giants, which [praised](https://substack.com/redirect/2ba15c6b-3733-4871-8676-ed1d33b152c8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) BAAJA as "essential to America's ability to build, compete, and lead--especially in the AI era." Advocates of BAAJA, [including Trump](https://substack.com/redirect/4c956583-4581-4e24-84cb-43e594e7d4f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), have tried to obscure this support by pointing to provisions in the legislation that would require data center developers to pay for the grid and transmission upgrades their projects require. But Americans have made overwhelmingly clear--not least through the massive victories they just handed to Democrats who pledged to support data center bans and moratoriums--that they don't just want AI data centers to help pay for some of their own costs. More than anything, they want the ability to say "no" to these monstrosities coming into their communities. They want to be able to decide their own futures, rather than having Big Tech billionaires make those decisions for them.
BAAJA is a direct response to this democratic backlash. AI corporations want to cut the public out of these decision-making processes, and BAAJA is laser-focused on overcoming the two most important roadblocks the public can use to check the explosion of Big Tech's data center build-out: permitting and easy access to fossil gas. (Abigail Dillen, the president of Earthjustice, recently [explained](https://substack.com/redirect/1a5e3ec5-ec3c-45ba-a2fb-cfaaa7ff1470?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) exactly how BAAJA enables "the dirtiest version of the data center build-out to move even faster.")
The antidemocratic betrayal here really cannot be overstated. Democrats just won their biggest congressional majorities in 50 years--to say nothing of victories in places like Texas, where Democrats swept every single statewide office and flipped the state House--in large part by promising to respond to the massive voter backlash against the AI industry's out-of-control expansion of hyperscale data centers. Just a week later, Democrats' Senate leadership team--not just Schumer but incoming Majority Whip Brian Schatz and DSCC chair Kirsten Gillibrand--joined Trump and the GOP to pass a catastrophic giveaway to the Big Tech billionaires who spent hundreds of millions of dollars trying to defeat their incoming colleagues, directly rebuking the massive voter mandate their party just received to stand up to those billionaires.
And that, maybe more than anything, helps explain the timing of this push. It's not just that BAAJA was developed without hearings or any of the other review procedures that a bill of this magnitude would normally go through. It's that Democrats like Whitehouse, Heinrich, Schumer, and Schatz are trying to ram this Project 2025 atrocity through a GOP-controlled lame-duck session weeks before Democrats take control. BAAJA advocates have argued that the legislation needs to move now because Trump would never sign a bill passed by a Democratic Congress, but that's an absurd claim. We have no idea how Trump will respond to the Democratic majority. There are myriad ways he could be brought to the table on a clean transmission bill--name the legislation after him, insert some shady Trump Organization business opportunity in the text, send in Zohran Mamdani to sell it ...
The reason top Senate Democrats are working to pass BAAJA now, before their majority is seated, is that this rotten handout to Big Oil and Big Tech--and massive "screw you" to the voters who just gave Democrats their majority--would never pass in a Democratic Congress. BAAJA is a radical MAGA bill that takes a sledgehammer to America's most important environmental laws, permanently locks us into an expansion of fossil fuels, disempowers local communities' ability to decide their own futures, and opens the door to a radical expansion of methane-powered hyperscale data centers. It needs to pass now because it is fundamentally a Republican bill.
BAAJA is on a fast track through the Senate, with a final vote only days away. But we must not accept this as a done deal. The Congressional Progressive Caucus, which represents more than 100 members of Congress, just announced its [opposition](https://substack.com/redirect/0494f2ec-3af3-4e8b-b405-d0a8d9397370?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the legislation. So did the Democratic attorneys general from California, Colorado, Delaware, Hawaii, Illinois, Maine, Maryland, Massachusetts, Michigan, Minnesota, Nevada, New York, Oregon, Vermont, Virginia, Washington, and Washington, D.C., who sent a [letter](https://substack.com/redirect/307d375d-967a-4d2c-bb98-75a622d18e0c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) asking Senate leadership to halt the upcoming votes on BAAJA in order to "protect our natural resources, historic and tribal sites, and state regulatory prerogatives." And it's not just elected officials who can weigh in. Everyone can make a difference by [calling and emailing their representatives and senators](https://substack.com/redirect/927444f9-16aa-42d9-9269-3917276bcc01?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and looking out for further [mobilization opportunities](https://substack.com/redirect/8cf42b38-1967-44ff-a668-f704b10fa40b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). If all else fails, at the very least, we must make sure that Democrats understand that their voters are paying attention to who is selling out our futures to Big Oil and Big Tech--and that 2028 is not so far away.

Peter, Last week, new member orientation started on Capitol Hill, and it was great to finally meet so many of the people who’ll be serving alongside me in the new Democratic majority. Congratulations to Randy Villegas, who will represent California’s very own Central Valley, Rebecca Cooke of Wisconsin, Ben McAdams of Utah, Daniel Biss of Illinois, Manny Rutinel of Colorado, Elaine Luria of Virginia, Christina Bohannan of Iowa, and Stefany Shaheen of New Hampshire. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143545292/660575412/-1807803310?refcode=em-11.16.26-all&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzAvMS85MDE1MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjMTM1ZGMyYi1kZmUxLWYxMTEtOTFmMC0wMDBkM2ExOGUyNDQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=MaU63kwl3BaoKtVCv5k0NSAMm5EcbbAWLgApobsxCSI=) Two years ago, I was the one sitting in those orientation sessions. Orientation is a crash course in how Congress works, and it moves fast. But what I remember most isn’t any of the briefings. It’s the feeling of walking into the Capitol knowing that thousands of people back home had put their trust in me, and that it was now my job to earn it. **That’s the same responsibility these new members are stepping into, and it’s one we’ll share.** When the 120th Congress is sworn in this January, we’ll have the power to hold this administration accountable, to push back when it overreaches, and to put forward a real agenda on the things people actually talk to me about: lowering costs, creating good-paying jobs, and making it possible for families to get ahead. I’m proud to be heading into this next Congress with such a strong group of new colleagues, and I’m grateful to have you with us too. Peter,

On Election Day, Michigan voters passed Proposal 2 with a whopping 81% of
the vote. It bans regulated utilities like DTE and Consumers Energy from
writing checks to Michigan politicians.

In short, it’s a huge step toward getting money out of politics.

We wish this were where the story ended, but just like clockwork, here
comes the corruption:

[ The ]The Detroit News: Consumers Energy, DTE seek to block 'Money Out Of
Politics' proposal

Now, the corporations that Michiganders voted to block from buying off
politicians are suing to make sure they can keep buying off politicians.

Prop 2 is set to take effect by December 3 unless a court blocks it.
Between now and then, DTE and Consumers need to see that
the people are

* * *
I'm a big believer in turning lemons into lemonade. Finding a little positive momentum in the middle of a bad situation.
So when I got stuck in Denver on Friday after the Trump administration's catastrophic, incompetent FAA ground stop, I decided pretty quickly that I wasn't going to waste the night. Instead of sitting in my hotel room seething and ranting about it on the internet, which, let's be honest, is what I usually do, I ended up playing poker with some friends,, meeting a bunch of new people at a happy hour, and closing out the night singing and dancing at a bar.
Not how I planned to spend my Friday, but not bad.
On Saturday I got to the Denver airport and found out my Chicago flight had been canceled again. Thousands of people across the country were in the same boat, all because this administration can't keep the planes in the air.
So I made another call. I bought a ticket to Omaha. If I couldn't get home to see my kid, I could at least go see my nieces and nephews, watch the Notre Dame game with my dad, and see my mom.
But here's the thing about life. My brother and I have a saying for this: right place, right time, wrong reason. It explains a lot about my life in particular.
When I got to my gate, I ran into Senator-elect Josh Turek from the great state of Iowa. I've had Josh on the show several times, and I've supported him basically since the day he launched his primary campaign last year.
We ended up sitting next to each other on the plane and talked the entire flight.
Most of that conversation is going to stay between him and me. But I'll tell you this much. Josh is one of the warmest, most thoughtful people I've met in politics.
I got to hear more of his personal story. He was born with spina bifida. He's had dozens of surgeries over the course of his life. And he became a Paralympic athlete anyway. The grit and resilience that takes is hard to even wrap your head around.
You walk away with the sense that this is a man who is going to fight for the least of us. Someone who is in this for the right reasons, in a way somebody with a more privileged path to power never could be.
Iowa elected a good man. And I got to see that up close, at 30,000 feet, because the Trump administration screwed up the entire national airspace on Friday.
Whatever the hell actually happened. A cyber attack. AI technology they rushed out before it was ready. Somebody cut a wire somewhere. I genuinely don't believe a word of what they're telling us. They have spent two years breaking things and lying about why, and Friday was just the latest example.
And that's what I keep coming back to this morning, writing to you from the airport again on my way to a two-day work trip.

Look at what these people have done over the last year or two. The chaos. The destruction. The corruption. The depravity. They meant all of it to wear us down. To make us tired and cynical enough to give up.
It hasn't worked.
Instead, they built a movement. They built this community, the one I get to talk with every single day. They built the anger and the energy that put Josh Turek in the Senate from a state that hasn't sent a Democrat there in a long time.
They built James Talarico. Annie Andrews. Scott Collum. Gina Hinojosa. So many others!
None of that is a gift from Donald Trump. It's what happens when people refuse to break.
Mark Manson has an idea I think about a lot from one of his books. He says the pursuit of the positive is itself a negative experience.
You don't get the good stuff by running away from the bad. You get it by walking straight through the bad, accepting what's in front of you, and doing something about it. Embrace the suck. That's what I tried to do this weekend, and it's what all of us have been doing for two years.
None of that makes me less angry about Friday.
I'm holding close to my heart the people who missed weddings. The people who missed funerals. The people who didn't make it to a loved one's bedside in time. Those people are hurting right now, and they deserve a hell of a lot better than an administration that can't keep the planes running and won't tell us the truth about why.
But I'm grateful, too.
I'm mad I didn't get to spend most of the weekend with my son. But I got a lovely afternoon with my nieces and nephews. I got a conversation with Iowa's next senator. And before all of this, I spent a few days at a very well put together conference in Denver, seeing people I love and meeting new people I hope I'll come to love.
So here's where I land on a Monday morning. I hope you all hit the ground running this week, and I hope none of you are stranded anywhere.
The last couple of weeks have brought some major wins, and also a stark series of reminders of how awful these people are. They're not going to stop. Neither are we.
Right place, right time, wrong reason. They gave us the wrong reason. We're the ones who decided to show up in the right place anyway.
With urgency,
--Mike

Dear Patriot,
Nearly twenty years in this work has taught me one rule about Washington: **When a door opens, someone is already pushing it shut.** Senator Rand Paul opened one for us. Send subpoena requests to his office . . . the one office in the Senate with sole power to issue them. **No reporter has ever held a key like this.** Since then, you and I have a responsibility to build something fast: A small team of researchers and professionals must be funded and put to work right now. Threads picked: the ballot cash. The border money. The Pfizer papers. And one twenty-year theory, at last ready for its test. Now for the truth about doors . . . Gavels change hands. Sessions end. And the first time a return comes back with a big name on it, they will push hard to shut this down. Harder than we have ever felt. **Senator Paul 's offer has no closing date printed on it. Washington will print one for us if we move slow.** So we will not move slow. | | Peter – On Friday, the Federal Aviation Administration grounded all flights in the United States because of "extraordinary circumstances." My support and thanks go to the staff at the FAA, every airline worker, flight crew, pilot, and airport staff for their hard work getting travelers back home. Safety _always_ comes first. I commend the quick action to address the issue. Domestic flights were grounded out of an abundance of caution after the air traffic control system overloaded. **But we cannot let this happen again.** The sudden chaos fueled misinformation and fear. Thousands of travelers were stranded across the country. With millions of Americans about to begin holiday travel, we need a clear solution. **My colleagues and I will press for answers on what happened and how we can keep it from happening again.** _Val_ |

clean_body: The FAA grounded flights because of "extraordinary circumstances." | | | | Peter – On Friday, the Federal Aviation Administration grounded all flights in the United States because of "extraordinary circumstances." My support and thanks go to the staff at the FAA, every airline worker, flight crew, pilot, and airport staff for their hard work getting travelers back home. Safety always comes first. I commend the quick action to address the issue. Domestic flights were grounded out of an abundance of caution after the air traffic control system overloaded. But we cannot let this happen again. The sudden chaos fueled misinformation and fear. Thousands of travelers were stranded across the country. With millions of Americans about to begin holiday travel, we need a clear solution. My colleagues and I will press for answers on what happened and how we can keep it from happening again. This is Rep. Patricia “Pat” Moore (D-LA).
Last week, Democrats won big. The House. The Senate. Seats in places nobody thought we could win.
But right now, the political world is asking one question: Was that the start of something, or a flash in the pan?
The answer won’t come from the pundits. It will come from the next races on the board, and the very first is my race.
_**On December 12, Louisiana’s 5th Congressional District goes to a runoff. I finished first. Now I have to finish the job.**_
History tells us exactly what’s at stake.
In 2008, Democrats rode a historic wave. Less than a month later, in a Georgia Senate runoff, our turnout dropped off and Republicans held the seat. A year after that, Republicans flipped Ted Kennedy’s old Senate seat in Massachusetts, and the far right came roaring back to take the House in 2010.
The lesson is simple: The moment we show weakness, they come roaring back.
If we win here we send a message to the entire country: Tuesday wasn’t the exception. It was the rule.
And we’ll make history doing it. If I win, I’ll be the FIRST Black woman Louisiana has ever sent to Congress.

Peter, **House Republicans just chose Jim Jordan as their new minority leader, and it tells you exactly where they plan to go as the minority in Congress.** Jordan is one of the most combative, hardline members of Congress, a Trump loyalist who built his reputation as a political attack dog, and his own allies say _that’s exactly why they picked him_. He has few friendships across the aisle, and **he’s made it clear he’s gearing up for all-out war with Democrats.** When he was asked about high gas prices, his answer was**“that’s life.”** Tell that to the farmers and families I talk to here in IL-17 who feel every one of those price hikes at the pump and at the grocery store, or the effects of the bill that cut Medicaid and food assistance to pay for tax breaks for the wealthy – _a bill that Jim Jordan championed._ But after twenty years of weather forecasting, I can tell you that **not every storm that looks scary on the radar is worth losing sleep over**. Voters just said they want a Congress that lowers costs and gets things done, and Democrats now have the numbers to deliver. Jim Jordan can give all the speeches he wants. He’s leading the minority, and a minority leader’s best weapon is _noise_. **So my plan hasn’t changed.** I’m going to keep working on lowering prescription drug and grocery costs, protecting health care, backing our family farmers, and holding this administration accountable. I’ll work with anyone, in either party, who’s serious about solving problems, and I won’t be distracted by anyone who’d rather put on a show. clean_body: | = Peter, House Republicans just chose Jim Jordan as their new minority leader, and it tells you exactly where they plan to go as the minority in Congress. Jordan is one of the most combative, hardline members of Congress, a Trump loyalist who built his reputation as a political attack dog, and his own allies say that’s exactly why they picked him. He has few friendships across the aisle, and he’s made it clear he’s gearing up for all-out war with Democrats. When he was asked about high gas prices, his answer was“that’s life.” Tell that to the farmers and families I talk to here in IL-17 who feel every one of those price hikes at the pump and at the grocery store, or the effects of the bill that cut Medicaid and food assistance to pay for tax breaks for the wealthy – a bill that Jim Jordan championed. But after twenty years of weather forecasting, I can tell you that not every storm that looks scary on the radar is worth losing sleep over. Voters just said they want a Congress that lowers costs and gets things done, and Democrats now have the numbers to deliver. Jim Jordan can give all the speeches he wants. He’s leading the minority, and a minority leader’s best weapon is noise. So my plan hasn’t changed. I’m going to keep working on lowering prescription drug and grocery costs, protecting health care, backing our family farmers, and holding this administration accountable. Last week, I asked what you want Congress to take on first once Democrats hold the majority in January, and hundreds of you have answered. My team and I are reading every response, including the long ones, and I wanted to share what we’re seeing so far:
* **Ending the war with Iran is out in front.** 87% of you want Congress to use a war powers resolution to bring it to an end.
* **Health care and food assistance are right behind it.** 84% want to reverse Trump’s Medicaid cuts, 78% want to reverse the SNAP cuts, and three in four want to extend the ACA tax credits that keep premiums down.
* **Tariffs and accountability are close behind.** 78% want the tariffs repealed, and 77% want this administration held accountable for corruption.
* **Costs are hitting hardest at the pump and on the utility bill.** Gas and utilities top the list, and when you write in your own answers, groceries come up more than anything else.

You want a Congress that does its job. Stop the war, bring costs down, and hold this administration accountable. Tariffs and accountability are close behind. 78% want the tariffs repealed, and 77% want this administration held accountable for corruption. Costs are hitting hardest at the pump and on the utility bill. Gas and utilities top the list, and when you write in your own answers, groceries come up more than anything else. You want a Congress that does its job. Stop the war, bring costs down, and hold this administration accountable. Come January, I intend to get to work on all of it. # [Singapore seized Nvidia-linked Spy CEO's passport for eight months ](https://substack.com/redirect/a5b808c0-2650-497d-8caa-d9d1d08c4b22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Singapore **[seized former Megaspeed CEO Alice Huang's passport](https://substack.com/redirect/cefc24ae-72ab-473a-afd7-788c33dee0fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in June 2025 and held it eight months while probing possible Nvidia chip routing to China, receiving limited assistance from U.S. authorities on supplier records.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a5b808c0-2650-497d-8caa-d9d1d08c4b22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Passport seized June 24** : Police took Huang's passport on June 24, 2025, after a Commerce voluntary shipment check and returned it February 26 after a warning and ban on her return.
* **Requests yielded limited aid** : Singapore sought Supermicro shipping records from July 7 for Malaysia-routed servers, escalating to repeated DOJ and FBI asks from September that produced limited information.
* **Commerce probe paused** : Investigators spent months on whether restricted AI chips reached China before Undersecretary Jeff Kessler reportedly stopped the case after Nvidia intervened; Justice continues the ongoing probe.
* **Supermicro and other trails** : Supermicro says it cooperated openly and was never a Megaspeed customer; separate Dell servers bought by Aperia in Singapore later showed Nvidia chips in a Shanghai loan filing.

---|---|---
* **Bessent sets deadline** : He told Fox the board should hire externally, questioned whether shell companies were obvious workarounds for China chip sales, and demanded answers from the board and outside counsel within 10 days while pinning Megaspeed's absence from the entity list on Commerce.
* **Petition and war room** : An open letter has drawn roughly 158,000 to 180,000 signatures including[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/d28a999f-f470-41b8-b233-c22bb6b71d48?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[Elon Musk and an Uber co-founder;](https://substack.com/redirect/d28a999f-f470-41b8-b233-c22bb6b71d48?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/d28a999f-f470-41b8-b233-c22bb6b71d48?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)the Financial Times reports Huang has discussed a return with confidantes while allies lobby the board and White House.
* **First post-Huang print** : Interim chief Colette Kress faces Tuesday's results, with Street forecasts around $109.1 billion in revenue, up 91 percent; options imply a 7.8 percent move, the largest in two years.
* **Stock and circulars** : Shares have fallen about 25 percent over the past month and erased roughly $1.7 trillion; Nvidia holds about $900 million in Side A D&O insurance but no Side B or Side C coverage, leaving $530 billion in commitments now resting on Kress.

# [Bitcoin crashes to $62k as $2B liquidations cascade](https://substack.com/redirect/a5b808c0-2650-497d-8caa-d9d1d08c4b22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Bitcoin **[tumbled to about $62,000 on Saturday,](https://substack.com/redirect/17931004-da1c-44d5-9967-f89de584463f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** its weakest since August and a sixth straight weekly decline, after breaking its 200-day moving average and triggering **[$1.3 billion to $2 billion in mostly long liquidations](https://substack.com/redirect/5fa382c4-c6b3-47ec-bef1-3fd88c1d01a6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** before a modest rebound.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a5b808c0-2650-497d-8caa-d9d1d08c4b22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Weekend low and rebound** : The token hit roughly $62,577 early Sunday, about 28 percent below its late-September peak near $87,162, then recovered toward $64,000 to $65,250 on Monday amid extreme fear.
* **ETF outflows and sentiment** : U.S. spot-bitcoin ETFs recorded six straight days of outflows; crypto-linked shares including Strategy and Coinbase fell as the token hovered near three-month lows.
* **Liquidation wave** : The break of the roughly $73,000 200-day average sparked the cascade; options traders are bracing for a slide toward $60,000.
* **Parallel pressure** : An industry expert **[noted the coming Anthropic IPO](https://substack.com/redirect/9ea68efc-3b34-441a-8bf5-c7be979d9f16?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** may be pulling demand from bitcoin ETFs, echoing patterns around prior listings.

# [Nvidia earnings and Anthropic IPO: AI's make-or-break week](https://substack.com/redirect/a5b808c0-2650-497d-8caa-d9d1d08c4b22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* **Yield backdrop** : The 10-year sat near 5.13 percent after last week's biggest yield jump since April 2025.
* **Strategist targets** : Goldman and Morgan Stanley both pencil in 8,700 for the S&P 500 by the end of 2027 on earnings growth and broader AI adoption.

The White House plans to name more than two dozen tech companies, including Nvidia, Amazon, and Microsoft, **[as AI national champions](https://substack.com/redirect/6cc90db8-b7e7-4cb2-ad49-8309b5fda0bc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in a program meant to help U.S. firms win business overseas.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a5b808c0-2650-497d-8caa-d9d1d08c4b22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Scope of the list** : The program covers Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI, and Anthropic among others, according to the Wall Street Journal.
* **Timing** : The designation comes days after Jensen Huang's resignation at Nvidia.
* **Purpose** : It aims to support U.S. AI companies competing internationally.
* **Market context** : The news arrives as Nvidia shares remain under pressure ahead of its earnings.

# [Nvidia's $530B commitments hang on interim CEO alone](https://substack.com/redirect/a5b808c0-2650-497d-8caa-d9d1d08c4b22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Nvidia's open checkbook for AI compute deals and startup investments is expected to tighten under interim CEO Colette Kress, with roughly $530 billion in[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/e8579d09-9c15-4794-be70-711d5ce78944?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[financial guarantees and supply commitments now hanging on her.](https://substack.com/redirect/e8579d09-9c15-4794-be70-711d5ce78944?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a5b808c0-2650-497d-8caa-d9d1d08c4b22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Scale of exposure** : Supply commitments and guarantees have swelled to about $530 billion, rising by nearly a quarter of a trillion dollars in a single quarter.
* **Leadership shift** : Huang himself had begun closing some windows months before the board ousted him, according to reporting.
* **Insurance gap** : The company has about $900 million in Side A directors-and-officers insurance but no Side B or Side C coverage for its own legal costs.
* **Earnings stakes** : Tuesday's results will be the first under Kress as the market tests whether the circular financing model holds.

body:
Mark is locked in a legal battle with the Secretary of Defense, and freedom of speech for every veteran in the United States is on the line.
#

Team,
Think back to this moment in 2024.
Donald Trump had just won re-election, Republicans would control the House and Senate, and the outlook for 2026 was grim. To have any chance at regaining some kind of power would require us to defend every Democratic Senator in office — and then flip several Republican seats, too.
Most people thought winning a majority in the Senate was an impossible task. Most, but not Mark Kelly.
He knew what was at stake for working families and took one of the most difficult jobs he could: Vice Chair of the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee. He was responsible for supporting the candidates who would take back the Senate. He hit the campaign trail across the country for Democrats in 23 states, and raised millions to help them hire staff, get their message out, and win.
And now, if Democrats win in Alaska, we’ll have a 56 member majority in the United States Senate. That’s what Mark does: He moves towards the fight, and he wins.
But the fight isn’t over. Mark is locked in a legal battle with the Secretary of Defense, with the freedom of speech rights of every veteran in the United States on the line. We can’t let him down.

body:
[ stdin# ]Josh Shapiro for Pennsylvania
I’ll be honest,
Derek: This email is going to look
a little different — and it’s going to be on the longer side. [ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/23416?t=1001&akid=959%2E245147%2EyBE7K4 ]So if
you’re short on time, please consider chipping in just a few bucks to make
sure we can keep moving our Commonwealth and country forward.

But if you have a few minutes, I hope you’ll keep reading.

Look, I’ve always tried to be the kind of Governor who looks toward the
future instead of the past. But I’ve been thinking about the state of our
country right now, and what history — in this case, ancient history — can
tell us about it.

Back in Caesar’s time, the wealthiest man in Rome was a guy named Crassus.
He created the first Roman fire brigade.

Whenever a fire broke out, they hurried to the site — but they didn’t put
the fire out.

Instead, they stood there, doing nothing — all while Crassus offered to
buy the burning property for pennies on the dollar. If the owner said yes,
they’d put out the fire. If they said no, they’d let it burn to the
ground.

Sure, this story is pretty ancient. But I think you can see the parallels
here in the present day just as clearly as I can.

Not only do we have our own Crassus in the White House. We have laws and
courts and a whole brigade of enablers and grifters allowing the fire to
spread.

Elected officials who do nothing while our economy’s in flames.

Tech companies that track where we go and what we do, so they can lease
our lives back to us for profit.

Private equity that sucks up our hospitals, daycares, even kids’ sports
leagues — extracting profit, and leaving us with the damage they leave
behind.

No, we didn’t quite extinguish the fire earlier this month on Election
Day. We’ve still got two more years of an arsonist in the White House. But
we did call in a new brigade — one that won’t just stand around, waiting
for orders from Donald Trump.

This moment calls for more than just strongly worded statements or
toothless half-measures. Leadership today has to be about how big we can
think. How tough we can fight.

That’s what we’ve done here in Pennsylvania.

Rebuilding I-95 in twelve days.

Standing up to energy companies that try to hike rates.

Criminally charging contractors that steal workers’ wages.

Stopping data centers from running roughshod over communities.

We cannot be limited by the status quo. Laws will need to change. And if
we have to amend the Constitution to make it happen, so be it.

That’s the kind of leadership the good people of Pennsylvania — and folks
all across the country — voted for earlier this month. But make no
mistake: The grifters and arsonists aren’t going to pack up and go home.
They’re going to fight us in every way they can. [ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/23416?t=1002&akid=959%2E245147%2EyBE7K4 ]And
Derek, that’s
exactly why I need to ask: Will you chip in just a few dollars to help us
keep up the fight for progress here in Pennsylvania? Every dollar counts
at an inflection point like this.

If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your
donation will go through immediately:

body:

| | | | | |

| |

My fellow Californians,
**Twice, California voters rejected attempts to abolish the death penalty. Twice, Sacramento was told NO.**
Yet Gavin Newsom is moving to overturn 548 death sentences handed down by juries who heard the evidence and delivered their verdicts.

These are convicted murderers, serial killers, child predators, and sadistic torturers. Monsters who kidnapped innocent children, subjected helpless victims to unimaginable suffering, and brutally extinguished innocent lives.
Their crimes represent the darkest depths of human cruelty and depravity. Behind every one of these atrocities are grieving parents, shattered families, and loved ones who have spent decades waiting for justice.
**Now Governor Newsom believes his judgment should outweigh the decisions of juries and the California voters.**
**The people have spoken. Sacramento needs to listen.**
As your Sheriff, I will always stand for victims, accountability, and the rule of law.

With gratitude,
**Sheriff Chad Bianco
Riverside County**

Look, there's a reason every border district from my home in South Texas to way up in Washington state went blue.
_This administration went too far on immigration enforcement._
They didn't just create chaos and fear within our communities. They tore the bottom out of our economy.
When people are too scared to show up at job sites, or when legal immigrants, including folks with green cards, step out of their homes and are pestered with questions by ICE, that's counterproductive.
The answer is clear to me, and I hope it's clear to this president: **We need immigration reform.**
I'm ready to talk with President Trump about a solution, and it doesn't have to wait until I'm sworn in.

body:
The bottom line is this: working hard ought to get you somewhere.

[ ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/143553536/660603560/510768709?refcode=email-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTIzMCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3MTlhNzIxNy1mNWUxLWYxMTEtOTFmMC0wMDBkM2ExOGUyNDQiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=LtFC5m7xm0zaUm9o09YH4QCLPyk74O0-Ti0qfTyn8Cc=) Hi there, On the campaign trail, I talked _a lot_ about what needs to change in our country and in Southwest Michigan, and don’t get me wrong, there is a lot. But today I wanted to take a moment and tell you what I’ll be fighting for on Day One. When I stepped up to run for Congress, it was out of the belief that our families deserve more — that hard work should pay off, that people should be able to get ahead and reach the American Dream, and that Washington should work for us, not the rich and well-connected. **In Congress, I’ll put partisan politics aside and focus on what matters to regular people here in Michigan’s Fourth.** Lowering the cost of gas and groceries. Ending chaotic tariffs that are raising prices everywhere. Expanding affordable healthcare, capping the cost of insulin and letting Medicare negotiate drug prices. Bringing the war with Iran to a close. Stopping corruption in Washington DC - prohibiting stock trading by members of Congress, the President and high-level officials. Passing policies to increase affordable housing so families can build a better life in Southwest Michigan. **The bottom line is: working hard ought to get you somewhere:** A home you can afford. Care when you’re sick. The ability to raise a thriving family. A retirement you can count on. Achieving the American Dream. That’s what I’m fighting for, because Southwest Michigan deserves nothing less. Look, you know I really don’t love asking for money, but here’s the deal: we won this race by fewer than 7,000 votes. It was **one of the most competitive races in the entire country,** and one of the most expensive. Our victory took everything we had. But we still need to close up the campaign office, pay our campaign staff, and make sure we’re ready to take office in just 48 days.
